items.title: Secret: Demo or default credentials displayed in UI code
items.description: A credential is written in the source code (value redacted).
items.recommendation: Remove it, rotate the credential, load it from an environment variable / secret store.

triage.explanation: The finding is in .cip-gitleaks.toml, which appears to be scanner configuration rather than application code or a live secret store. Demo/default credentials referenced in detection rules are commonly test patterns, not usable credentials.
triage.fix: Confirm the value is only a detection example/config artifact; if so, suppress this rule hit. If it is a real credential, remove it and rotate it.

items.title: Secret: Hardcoded database connection string with credentials
items.description: A credential is written in the source code (value redacted).
items.recommendation: Remove it, rotate the credential, load it from an environment variable / secret store.

triage.explanation: This is also reported in .cip-gitleaks.toml, suggesting the scanner matched its own rule/config text rather than an application secret. Unless that file contains an actual live connection string, this is not an exploitable application issue.
triage.fix: Verify the matched content is only rule text or a redacted example, then suppress/allowlist it. If a real connection string exists, remove it from source and rotate database credentials.

items.title: Secret: Hardcoded username or login name in source code
items.description: A credential is written in the source code (value redacted).
items.recommendation: Remove it, rotate the credential, load it from an environment variable / secret store.

triage.explanation: A hardcoded username in frontend source is often a placeholder, demo value, or validation string rather than a secret by itself. However, if it corresponds to a real privileged account used by the app, it can aid credential stuffing or reveal operational details.
triage.fix: Check whether the value is a real account identifier; if so, remove it from client code, move configuration server-side, and rotate associated credentials if used with a real password.

items.title: Secret: Hardcoded password in source code
items.description: A credential is written in the source code (value redacted).
items.recommendation: Remove it, rotate the credential, load it from an environment variable / secret store.

triage.explanation: A hardcoded password in src/constants.js is high risk because frontend source is distributed to users and any embedded secret is effectively public. If this password is used for any real environment, account, API, or demo backend, it must be treated as compromised.
triage.fix: Remove the password from client code immediately, move secret handling to a backend or environment-managed secret store, and rotate the exposed credential.

items.title: Secret: Hardcoded username or login name in source code

triage.fix: Upgrade tinypool to >=2.1.2 everywhere in the dependency tree; if only used by test tooling, keep it out of production images and lock dev tooling to patched versions.

spec.title: Security scan
spec.why: Find vulnerable code (SAST), vulnerable dependencies (SCA), leaked secrets and misconfigurations before anything is built or shipped.

spec.title: HITL – review security reports
spec.why: A human reviews the scan reports and the security gate result, then approves (the pipeline continues) or rejects (the pipeline stops and reports).

spec.title: Build · unit tests · package · containerise
spec.why: Compile every component with its own toolchain, prove it works with unit tests, then package it (and build + scan its image).

spec.title: Release to registry
spec.why: Publish the tested image under a fixed tag so every later environment deploys exactly the same artifact.

spec.title: Deploy to dev
spec.why: Run the released images together on a private network to see the application start and answer requests.

spec.title: Functional tests
spec.why: Exercise the running application like a user would – pages, API endpoints and AI-proposed journeys.

spec.title: UI browser tests
spec.why: Use the running application in a real browser (Selenium + headless Chrome) – pages render with their JavaScript, no console errors, navigation and forms work, AI-written user journeys succeed – with a screenshot of every check.

spec.title: Publish test results

spec.title: Approval before UAT
spec.why: A human reviews the stage reports and decides whether the build may go to UAT.

spec.title: Deploy to UAT
spec.why: Run the released images in the UAT environment (separate network and ports) for acceptance testing.

items.title: react-router 6.30.4 – react-router: React Router: Open Redirect vulnerability via backslashes in navigation components
items.description: React Router is a router for React. Versions 6.0.0 through 7.17.0 are vulnerable to Open Redirtect through use of backslashes in <Link> and useNavigate. This issue is a follow up to CVE-2025-68470 and has been fixed in version 7.18.0.

items.title: react-router-dom 6.30.4 – react-router: react-router-dom: React Router: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via open redirects
items.description: React Router is a router for React. In versions 6.30.2 through 6.30.4 and 7.9.6 through 7.12.0, applications that allow open redirects are vulnerable to XSS. An attacker could craft a malicious link that redirects users to an unexpected external site or that exploits an XSS vector.This issue has been fixed in version 7.13.0.

items.title: uuid 10.0.0 – uuid: uuid: Out-of-bounds write vulnerability impacts data integrity and confidentiality
items.description: uuid is for the creation of RFC9562 (formerly RFC4122) UUIDs. Prior to 14.0.0, v3, v5, and v6 accept external output buffers but do not reject out-of-range writes (small buf or large offset). This allows silent partial writes into caller-provided buffers. This vulnerability is fixed in 14.0.0.

items.title: xlsx 0.18.5 – Prototype Pollution in sheetJS
items.description: SheetJS Community Edition before 0.19.3 allows Prototype Pollution via a crafted file. In other words. 0.19.2 and earlier are affected, whereas 0.19.3 and later are unaffected.

triage.explanation: The application includes xlsx 0.18.5, which is within the vulnerable range for SheetJS prototype pollution. If the app parses attacker-controlled spreadsheet files, this can lead to object property injection and potentially unsafe application behavior.
triage.fix: Upgrade xlsx to 0.19.3 or later; preferably move to the latest available version that also addresses newer issues. Until upgraded, do not process untrusted spreadsheet files or isolate parsing in a hardened sandbox.

items.title: xlsx 0.18.5 – SheetJS Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS)
items.description: SheetJS Community Edition before 0.20.2 is vulnerable.to Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS).

triage.explanation: The application includes xlsx 0.18.5, which is affected by the SheetJS ReDoS issue. If users can supply crafted spreadsheet content, parsing may consume excessive CPU and cause a denial of service.
triage.fix: Upgrade xlsx to 0.20.2 or later. As a temporary mitigation, restrict or reject untrusted spreadsheet uploads, enforce file size and processing time limits, and perform parsing in a separate worker/process with resource limits.

spec.title: Security scan
spec.why: Find vulnerable code (SAST), vulnerable dependencies (SCA), leaked secrets and misconfigurations before anything is built or shipped.

spec.title: HITL – review security reports
spec.why: A human reviews the scan reports and the security gate result, then approves (the pipeline continues) or rejects (the pipeline stops and reports).

spec.title: Build · unit tests · package · containerise
spec.why: Compile every component with its own toolchain, prove it works with unit tests, then package it (and build + scan its image).

spec.title: Release to registry
spec.why: Publish the tested image under a fixed tag so every later environment deploys exactly the same artifact.

spec.title: Deploy to dev
spec.why: Run the released images together on a private network to see the application start and answer requests.

spec.title: Functional tests
spec.why: Exercise the running application like a user would – pages, API endpoints and AI-proposed journeys.

spec.title: UI browser tests
spec.why: Use the running application in a real browser (Selenium + headless Chrome) – pages render with their JavaScript, no console errors, navigation and forms work, AI-written user journeys succeed – with a screenshot of every check.

spec.title: Publish test results
spec.why: Collect every test result of the run into one report (JUnit XML + HTML) that can be attached to the release / user story.

spec.title: Approval before UAT
spec.why: A human reviews the stage reports and decides whether the build may go to UAT.

spec.title: Deploy to UAT
spec.why: Run the released images in the UAT environment (separate network and ports) for acceptance testing.

spec.title: Final report
spec.why: Decide the overall result from the gates, explain the root cause and write the PDF report.

items.description: React Router is a router for React. This is only possible with very specific (and unlikely) application-layer code. Note that this does not impact an application if it is using Declarative Mode. items.title: react-router 6.30.4 – react-router: React Router: Open Redirect vulnerability via backslashes in navigation components
items.description: React Router is a router for React. Versions 6.0.0 through 7.17.0 are vulnerable to Open Redirtect through use of backslashes in <Link> and useNavigate. This issue is a follow up to CVE-2025-68470 and has been fixed in version 7.18.0.

items.title: react-router-dom 6.30.4 – react-router: react-router-dom: React Router: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via open redirects
items.description: React Router is a router for React. In versions 6.30.2 through 6.30.4 and 7.9.6 through 7.12.0, applications that allow open redirects are vulnerable to XSS. An attacker could craft a malicious link that redirects users to an unexpected external site or that exploits an XSS vector.This issue has been fixed in version 7.13.0.

items.title: uuid 10.0.0 – uuid: uuid: Out-of-bounds write vulnerability impacts data integrity and confidentiality
items.description: uuid is for the creation of RFC9562 (formerly RFC4122) UUIDs. Prior to 14.0.0, v3, v5, and v6 accept external output buffers but do not reject out-of-range writes (small buf or large offset). This allows silent partial writes into caller-provided buffers. This vulnerability is fixed in 14.0.0.

items.title: xlsx 0.18.5 – Prototype Pollution in sheetJS
items.description: SheetJS Community Edition before 0.19.3 allows Prototype Pollution via a crafted file. In other words. 0.19.2 and earlier are affected, whereas 0.19.3 and later are unaffected.

triage.explanation: The application includes xlsx 0.18.5, which is within the vulnerable range for SheetJS prototype pollution. If the app parses untrusted spreadsheet files, a crafted workbook could tamper with object prototypes and impact application logic or downstream security controls.
triage.fix: Upgrade xlsx to 0.19.3 or later, preferably to the latest available version. Also treat uploaded/imported spreadsheet files as untrusted input and avoid merging parsed data into plain objects without defensive cloning or key filtering.

items.title: xlsx 0.18.5 – SheetJS Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS)
items.description: SheetJS Community Edition before 0.20.2 is vulnerable.to Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS).

triage.explanation: The dependency version xlsx 0.18.5 is also affected by the reported ReDoS issue. If users can supply spreadsheet content for parsing, an attacker may be able to cause excessive CPU consumption and degrade availability during file import or processing.
triage.fix: Upgrade xlsx to 0.20.2 or later, ideally the latest release that includes both fixes. As a defense-in-depth measure, enforce file size/time limits and process spreadsheet imports with resource constraints.

items.title: c-ares 1.34.5-r0 – c-ares: c-ares: Use-after-free / double-free in query-completion handling
items.description: c-ares is an asynchronous resolver library. From ver 1.32.3 until 1.34.7, a use-after-free / double-free in c-ares' query-completion handling. The same flaw — a query's callback being invoked while the query is still linked in the channel's internal lookup structures — is present at multiple points in the resend/finish path (timeout handling, response handling, and query dispatch). If the query, or for ares_getaddrinfo() the owning host_query, is freed as a side effect of that callback, it is then accessed and/or freed a second time. This vulnerability is fixed in ver 1.34.7.

items.title: c-ares 1.34.5-r0 – c-ares: c-ares: Denial of Service due to query termination after maximum attempts
items.description: c-ares is an asynchronous resolver library. Versions 1.32.3 through 1.34.5  terminate a query after maximum attempts when using read_answer() and process_answer(), which can cause a Denial of Service. This issue is fixed in version 1.34.6.

items.title: curl 8.12.1-r1 – libcurl: curl: QUIC certificate check skip with wolfSSL
items.description: libcurl accidentally skips the certificate verification for QUIC connections when connecting to a host specified as an IP address in the URL. Therefore, it does not detect impostors or man-in-the-middle attacks.

items.title: curl 8.12.1-r1 – curl: libcurl: QUIC Certificate Pinning Bypass
items.description: libcurl supports *pinning* of the server certificate public key for HTTPS transfers. Due to an omission, this check is not performed when connecting with QUIC for HTTP/3, when the TLS backend is wolfSSL. Documentation says the option works with wolfSSL, failing to specify that it does not for QUIC and HTTP/3. Since pinning makes the transfer succeed if the pin is fine, users could unwittingly connect to an impostor server without noticing.

items.title: curl 8.12.1-r1 – curl: libcurl: WebSocket endless loop
items.description:
Due to a mistake in libcurl's WebSocket code, a malicious server can send a
particularly crafted packet which makes libcurl get trapped in an endless
busy-loop.

There is no other way for the application to escape or exit this loop other
than killing the thread/process.

This might be used to DoS libcurl-using application.

items.title: curl 8.12.1-r1 – curl: predictable WebSocket mask
items.description:
curl's WebSocket code did not update the 32-bit mask pattern for each new
outgoing frame as the specification says. Instead it used a fixed mask that
persisted and was used throughout the entire connection.

A predictable mask pattern allows for a malicious server to induce traffic
between the two communicating parties that could be interpreted by an involved
proxy (configured or transparent) as genuine, real, HTTP traffic with content
and thereby poison its cache. That cached poisoned content could then be
served to all users of that proxy.

items.description: libcurl supports *pinning* of the server certificate public key for HTTPS transfers. Due to an omission, this check is not performed when connecting with QUIC for HTTP/3, when the TLS backend is wolfSSL. Documentation says the option works with wolfSSL, failing to specify that it does not for QUIC and HTTP/3. Since pinning makes the transfer succeed if the pin is fine, users could unwittingly connect to an impostor server without noticing.

items.title: libcurl 8.12.1-r1 – curl: libcurl: WebSocket endless loop
items.description:
Due to a mistake in libcurl's WebSocket code, a malicious server can send a
particularly crafted packet which makes libcurl get trapped in an endless
busy-loop.

There is no other way for the application to escape or exit this loop other
than killing the thread/process.

This might be used to DoS libcurl-using application.

items.title: libcurl 8.12.1-r1 – curl: libcurl: Curl out of bounds read for cookie path
items.description:
1. A cookie is set using the `secure` keyword for `https://target`
2. curl is redirected to or otherwise made to speak with `http://target` (same
   hostname, but using clear text HTTP) using the same cookie set
3. The same cookie name is set - but with only a slash as path (`path="/"`).
   Since this site is not secure, the cookie *should* be ignored.
4. A bug in the path comparison logic makes curl read outside a heap buffer
   boundary

The bug either causes a crash or it potentially makes the comparison come to

items.title: libcurl 8.12.1-r1 – curl: predictable WebSocket mask
items.description:
curl's WebSocket code did not update the 32-bit mask pattern for each new
outgoing frame as the specification says. Instead it used a fixed mask that
persisted and was used throughout the entire connection.

A predictable mask pattern allows for a malicious server to induce traffic
between the two communicating parties that could be interpreted by an involved
proxy (configured or transparent) as genuine, real, HTTP traffic with content
and thereby poison its cache. That cached poisoned content could then be
served to all users of that proxy.

items.description: Expat through 2.8.3 contains a denial of service vulnerability caused by quadratic algorithmic complexity in the storeAtts() function in xmlparse.c, where processing N specified attributes with non-normalized values triggers an O(N^2) linear scan of elementType->defaultAtts to determine CDATA status. A remote unauthenticated attacker can supply a single well-formed XML document of a few megabytes to an application parsing untrusted XML to cause excessive CPU consumption, resulting in denial of service without requiring authentication, external entity resolution, or non-default parser options.

A struct size mismatch between ELEMENT_TYPE members causes storeAtts to read the attIndex member past allocated memory boundaries, resulting in failure to normalize whitespace in non-CDATA attributes or a wild pointer dereference causing a segfault. This vulnerability was introduced by the fix for CVE-2026-66046.

items.title: libpng 1.6.47-r0 – libpng: LIBPNG buffer overflow
items.description: LIBPNG is a reference library for use in applications that read, create, and manipulate PNG (Portable Network Graphics) raster image files. From version 1.6.0 to before 1.6.51, an out-of-bounds read vulnerability exists in png_image_read_composite when processing palette images with PNG_FLAG_OPTIMIZE_ALPHA enabled. The palette compositing code in png_init_read_transformations incorrectly applies background compositing during premultiplication, violating the invariant component ≤ alpha × 257 required by the simplified PNG API. This issue has been patched in version 1.6.51.

Attacker-crafted interlaced PNG files cause heap writes beyond allocated buffer bounds. This issue has been patched in version 1.6.51.

--- self-healing attempt 1 (image CVEs, 2 critical / 39 high) ---
Updated `Dockerfile` to use a newer patch tag in the same image family and upgrade Alpine packages in the final image:

```dockerfile
FROM nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:1.27.5-alpine

RUN apk upgrade --no-cache

COPY dist/ /usr/share/nginx/html/
EXPOSE 8080
```

ROOT CAUSE: The image was based on an older `nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:1.27-alpine` variant that included vulnerable Alpine runtime packages (e.g. `libcrypto3`, `libssl3`, `musl`, `zlib`, `libxml2`) with fixes already available upstream.

FIX: Bumped the base image to a newer patch release in the same `1.27-alpine` family and added `apk upgrade --no-cache` so the final image pulls in the fixed Alpine package versions while keeping the same port and runtime behavior.
(the hardened Dockerfile did not build – reverted to the previous one)

Updated the Dockerfile to use a newer patch/minor image in the same family and to upgrade Alpine packages in the final image so fixed OS/runtime package versions are installed.

```dockerfile
FROM nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:1.29-alpine

RUN apk upgrade --no-cache

COPY dist/ /usr/share/nginx/html/
EXPOSE 8080
```

spec.title: Security scan

spec.title: Build · unit tests · package · containerise
spec.why: Compile every component with its own toolchain, prove it works with unit tests, then package it (and build + scan its image).

spec.title: Release to registry
spec.why: Publish the tested image under a fixed tag so every later environment deploys exactly the same artifact.

spec.title: Deploy to dev
spec.why: Run the released images together on a private network to see the application start and answer requests.

spec.title: Functional tests
spec.why: Exercise the running application like a user would – pages, API endpoints and AI-proposed journeys.

spec.title: UI browser tests
spec.why: Use the running application in a real browser (Selenium + headless Chrome) – pages render with their JavaScript, no console errors, navigation and forms work, AI-written user journeys succeed – with a screenshot of every check.

spec.title: Publish test results
spec.why: Collect every test result of the run into one report (JUnit XML + HTML) that can be attached to the release / user story.

spec.title: Approval before UAT
spec.why: A human reviews the stage reports and decides whether the build may go to UAT.

spec.title: Deploy to UAT
spec.why: Run the released images in the UAT environment (separate network and ports) for acceptance testing.

triage.explanation: A scanner found a password-like value in client-side JavaScript. If this is a real credential, shipping it in source exposes it to anyone who can access the bundle; however, validator files often contain test strings or regex examples that can trigger false positives.
triage.fix: Inspect src/utils/validators.js line 324 to determine whether the value is an actual secret or only a sample/test constant. If it is real, remove it from source, rotate the credential, and load secrets from a server-side secret manager or environment variable instead of client code.

--- self-healing attempt 1 (image CVEs, 2 critical / 39 high) ---
Updated `Dockerfile` to use a newer patch tag in the same image family and upgrade Alpine packages in the final image while preserving the exposed port and runtime user.

```dockerfile
FROM nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:1.27.5-alpine

USER root
RUN apk upgrade --no-cache
USER nginx

COPY dist/ /usr/share/nginx/html/
EXPOSE 8080
```

ROOT CAUSE: The image was based on an older `nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:1.27-alpine` tag containing vulnerable Alpine OS/runtime packages (e.g. `libcrypto3`, `libssl3`, `musl`, `zlib`) with newer fixed versions already available.

FIX: Bumped the base image to a newer patch release in the same family (`1.27.5-alpine`) and added `apk upgrade --no-cache` in the final stage to pull in patched Alpine packages, while keeping the same port and nginx user.

spec.title: Security scan
spec.why: Find vulnerable code (SAST), vulnerable dependencies (SCA), leaked secrets and misconfigurations before anything is built or shipped.

spec.title: HITL – review security reports
spec.why: A human reviews the scan reports and the security gate result, then approves (the pipeline continues) or rejects (the pipeline stops and reports).

spec.title: Build · unit tests · package · containerise
spec.why: Compile every component with its own toolchain, prove it works with unit tests, then package it (and build + scan its image).

spec.title: Release to registry
spec.why: Publish the tested image under a fixed tag so every later environment deploys exactly the same artifact.

spec.title: Deploy to dev
spec.why: Run the released images together on a private network to see the application start and answer requests.

spec.title: Functional tests
spec.why: Exercise the running application like a user would – pages, API endpoints and AI-proposed journeys.

spec.title: UI browser tests
spec.why: Use the running application in a real browser (Selenium + headless Chrome) – pages render with their JavaScript, no console errors, navigation and forms work, AI-written user journeys succeed – with a screenshot of every check.

spec.title: Publish test results
spec.why: Collect every test result of the run into one report (JUnit XML + HTML) that can be attached to the release / user story.

spec.title: Approval before UAT
spec.why: A human reviews the stage reports and decides whether the build may go to UAT.

spec.title: Deploy to UAT
spec.why: Run the released images in the UAT environment (separate network and ports) for acceptance testing.

spec.title: Final report
spec.why: Decide the overall result from the gates, explain the root cause and write the PDF report.

image.writespace.explanation:
--- self-healing attempt 1 (docker build) ---
Updated the Dockerfile to build the Vite app inside Docker and copy the generated `dist/` output into nginx, instead of trying to copy hard-coded asset filenames from the repo root.

ROOT CAUSE: The Dockerfile expected prebuilt Vite artifacts (`favicon.svg`, `index-Cn_TbKHe.css`, `index-DMZ2Grak.js`) to exist at the repository root, but this repo contains source files, not built output. Vite generates hashed asset names at build time under `dist/`, so those hard-coded filenames were missing from the Docker build context.

FIX: Replaced the static-file COPY steps with a multi-stage Docker build:
1. Use `node:20-alpine` to run `npm ci` and `npm run build`
2. Copy `/app/dist/` into the nginx web root
3. Keep the existing nginx SPA config and non-root runtime setup
--- self-healing attempt 1 (image CVEs, 2 critical / 41 high) ---
Updated the Dockerfile to use a newer nginx patch tag in the same family and to upgrade Alpine packages in both stages so fixed OS/runtime packages are pulled into the final image.

ROOT CAUSE: The image was built from older Alpine-based Node/Nginx layers that contained vulnerable package versions (for example libssl3/libcrypto3 3.3.3-r0), and the Dockerfile did not upgrade installed OS packages during build.
FIX: Bumped the final base image from `nginx:1.27-alpine` to `nginx:1.27.5-alpine` and added `apk upgrade --no-cache` to refresh installed Alpine packages to fixed versions while preserving the same port, user, and start command.
RESULT: 2 critical / 41 high → 0 critical / 0 high CVEs after the rebuild

deploy.explanation:
--- writespace: self-healing attempt 1 (deploy) ---
Updated the Dockerfile to run nginx as its default user instead of forcing a non-root user that lacks permission to create `/run/nginx.pid`.

ROOT CAUSE: The container switched to `USER app`, but nginx still used its default pid path `/run/nginx.pid`; that non-root user could not write there, so nginx exited immediately with `open() "/run/nginx.pid" failed (13: Permission denied)`.

FIX: Removed the custom non-root user override and kept nginx running with its default startup behavior, while preserving the app’s static site config on port `5173` (`listen 5173;` and `EXPOSE 5173`).
RESULT: redeployed → passed (answered HTTP 200) http://127.0.0.1:49562

--- writespace: self-healing attempt 1 (deploy) ---
Updated the Dockerfile so nginx explicitly listens on `0.0.0.0:5173`, matching the expected exposed port.

ROOT CAUSE: nginx was started successfully, but the custom config only used `listen 5173;`, which can be ambiguous for platform health checks expecting an explicit bind on `0.0.0.0:5173`.  
FIX: changed the nginx server config in the Dockerfile to `listen 0.0.0.0:5173;` while keeping `EXPOSE 5173` and the existing static SPA setup unchanged.
RESULT: redeployed → failed (did not become healthy) http://0.0.0.0:52216
--- writespace: self-healing attempt 2 (deploy) ---
The container is starting nginx successfully, so this is not a crash, missing file, or bad start command issue.

The likely problem is the nginx `listen` directive in the custom config:

```nginx
listen 0.0.0.0:5173;
```

In nginx, `listen` should normally be declared as just the port (or `IP:port` in forms nginx accepts). Using `0.0.0.0:5173` here is unnecessary and can cause the service not to be exposed the way the platform health check expects. The standard nginx way to listen on all interfaces is:

```nginx
listen 5173;
listen [::]:5173;
```

I updated the Dockerfile to use a standard nginx server block while keeping the app behavior unchanged and still serving on port `5173`.

Updated `Dockerfile`:
```dockerfile
FROM node:20-alpine AS build
WORKDIR /app

RUN apk upgrade --no-cache

COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
RUN npm ci

COPY . .
RUN npm run build

FROM nginx:1.27.5-alpine

RUN apk upgrade --no-cache

RUN rm -f /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf
RUN printf 'server {\n    listen 5173;\n    listen [::]:5173;\n    server_name _;\n    root /usr/share/nginx/html;\n    index index.html;\n\n    location / {\n        try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html;\n    }\n\n    location /assets/ {\n        try_files $uri =404;\n        expires 1y;\n        add_header Cache-Control "public, immutable";\n    }\n}\n' > /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf

COPY --from=build /app/dist/ /usr/share/nginx/html/

EXPOSE 5173

CMD ["nginx", "-g", "daemon off;"]
```

ROOT CAUSE: Custom nginx config used a nonstandard `listen 0.0.0.0:5173;` directive, so the service was not listening in the expected way for the platform health check on port 5173.  
FIX: Changed nginx to listen with `listen 5173;` and `listen [::]:5173;`, keeping `EXPOSE 5173` and the existing nginx start command.

--------------------

spec.title: Security scan

spec.title: Build · unit tests · package · containerise
spec.why: Compile every component with its own toolchain, prove it works with unit tests, then package it (and build + scan its image).

spec.title: Release to registry
spec.why: Publish the tested image under a fixed tag so every later environment deploys exactly the same artifact.

spec.title: Deploy to dev
spec.why: Run the released images together on a private network to see the application start and answer requests.

spec.title: Functional tests
spec.why: Exercise the running application like a user would – pages, API endpoints and AI-proposed journeys.

spec.title: UI browser tests
spec.why: Use the running application in a real browser (Selenium + headless Chrome) – pages render with their JavaScript, no console errors, navigation and forms work, AI-written user journeys succeed – with a screenshot of every check.

spec.title: Publish test results

spec.why: A human reviews the stage reports and decides whether the build may go to UAT.

items.title: @remix-run/router 1.23.2 – react-router: React Router: Open redirect vulnerability via specially crafted URLs
items.description: React Router is a router for React. In versions 7.0.0 through 7.14.0 and 6.7.0 through 6.30.3, certain URLs passed to the redirect function can trigger an open redirect to an external domain due to path values starting with // being reinterpreted as protocol-relative URLs. The level of impact depends on the validation done by the application prior to returning the redirect. This does not impact applications using Declarative Mode (<BrowserRouter>). This is patched in versions 7.14.1 and 6.30.4.

items.title: dompurify 2.5.9 – dompurify: Mutation XSS in DOMPurify Due to Improper Template Literal Handling
items.description: DOMPurify before 3.2.4 has an incorrect template literal regular expression, sometimes leading to mutation cross-site scripting (mXSS).

items.title: dompurify 2.5.9 – DOMPurify: Vue 2: DOMPurify: Cross-site scripting due to incomplete sanitization of template expressions
items.description: DOMPurify is a DOM-only cross-site scripting sanitizer for HTML, MathML, and SVG. Starting in version 1.0.10 and prior to version 3.4.0, `SAFE_FOR_TEMPLATES` strips `{{...}}` expressions from untrusted HTML. This works in string mode but not with `RETURN_DOM` or `RETURN_DOM_FRAGMENT`, allowing XSS via template-evaluating frameworks like Vue 2. Version 3.4.0 patches the issue.

items.title: dompurify 2.5.9 – DOMPurify: DOMPurify: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via inconsistent tag sanitization
items.description: DOMPurify is a DOM-only cross-site scripting sanitizer for HTML, MathML, and SVG. Versions prior to 3.4.0 have an inconsistency between FORBID_TAGS and FORBID_ATTR handling when function-based ADD_TAGS is used. Commit c361baa added an early exit for FORBID_ATTR at line 1214. The same fix was not applied to FORBID_TAGS. At line 1118-1123, when EXTRA_ELEMENT_HANDLING.tagCheck returns true, the short-circuit evaluation skips the FORBID_TAGS check entirely. This allows forbidden elements to survive sanitization with their attributes intact. Version 3.4.0 patches the issue.

items.title: dompurify 2.5.9 – dompurify: DOMPurify: Cross-site scripting due to improper sanitization of DOM nodes
items.description: DOMPurify is a DOM-only cross-site scripting sanitizer for HTML, MathML, and SVG. Prior to 3.4.6, DOMPurify.sanitize(node, { IN_PLACE: true }) accepted same-origin foreign-realm DOM nodes while follow-on checks used parent-realm constructors, causing instanceof checks for forms, named node maps, document fragments, and elements to fail and skip clobber, template-content, and shadow-DOM sanitization branches so executable markup could survive. This issue is fixed in version 3.4.6.

items.title: dompurify 2.5.9 – dompurify: DOMPurify: Cross-site scripting bypass allows arbitrary script execution
items.description: DOMPurify is a DOM-only cross-site scripting sanitizer for HTML, MathML, and SVG. Prior to 3.4.6, DOMPurify.sanitize(root, { IN_PLACE: true }) could preserve event-handler attributes on an attacker-controlled <form> root when a descendant name clobbered properties checked by _isClobbered, because _forceRemove no-opped on the parent-less root and _sanitizeAttributes returned early. This issue is fixed in version 3.4.6.

items.title: dompurify 2.5.9 – dompurify: DOMPurify: Cross-site scripting vulnerability allows code execution
items.description: DOMPurify is a DOM-only cross-site scripting sanitizer for HTML, MathML, and SVG. Prior to 3.4.7, DOMPurify IN_PLACE sanitization could skip shadow contents attached to an element inside <template>.content, allowing attacker-controlled markup such as event handlers, JavaScript URLs, or scripts to survive and execute when an application cloned and inserted the sanitized template. This issue is fixed in version 3.4.7.

items.title: dompurify 2.5.9 – dompurify: DOMPurify: Cross-site scripting via permanent attribute allowlist pollution
items.description: DOMPurify before 3.4.11 fails to clone the ALLOWED_ATTR allowlist when setConfig() is used with an uponSanitizeAttribute hook, allowing the hook to permanently mutate the shared allowlist. Attackers can register a hook that conditionally allows dangerous attributes like onerror for trusted elements, then submit untrusted content that inherits the polluted allowlist and executes event handlers as stored XSS.

items.title: dompurify 2.5.9 – dompurify: DOMPurify: Sanitization bypass via hook manipulation
items.description: DOMPurify before 3.4.7 (affected versions <= 3.4.5) passes direct references to the module-level DEFAULT_ALLOWED_TAGS and DEFAULT_ALLOWED_ATTR sets to the uponSanitizeElement and uponSanitizeAttribute hooks via data.allowedTags / data.allowedAttributes when sanitize is called without an explicit cfg.ALLOWED_TAGS / cfg.ALLOWED_ATTR array. A hook that mutates these fields permanently widens the default allow-lists for the lifetime of the DOMPurify instance, so all subsequent default-config sanitize calls inherit the widened defaults and attacker payloads using the poisoned tag/attribute name sur

items.title: dompurify 2.5.9 – dompurify: DOMPurify: Security bypass allows injection of malicious content
items.description: DOMPurify before 3.4.0 contains a logic error in the ADD_TAGS function where short-circuit evaluation allows forbidden tags to bypass FORBID_TAGS restrictions. Attackers can craft input containing tags listed in FORBID_TAGS that are also added via ADD_TAGS function, causing them to be retained in sanitized output.

items.title: dompurify 2.5.9 – dompurify: DOMPurify: URI validation bypass leads to cross-site scripting
items.description: DOMPurify before 3.3.2 contains a URI validation bypass vulnerability when ADD_ATTR is provided as a predicate function via EXTRA_ELEMENT_HANDLING.attributeCheck. Attackers can supply a predicate that accepts specific attribute and tag combinations to bypass URI-safe validation, allowing unsafe protocols like javascript: to survive sanitization and execute as DOM-based XSS when the link is activated.

items.title: dompurify 2.5.9 – dompurify: DOMPurify: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via prototype pollution in USE_PROFILES mode
items.description: DOMPurify before 3.3.2 contains a prototype pollution vulnerability in USE_PROFILES mode that allows attackers to bypass attribute filtering by polluting Array.prototype properties. Attackers can set Array.prototype properties like onclick to true, causing DOMPurify to accept event handlers as allowlisted attributes and resulting in DOM-based XSS when sanitized markup is rendered.

items.title: dompurify 2.5.9 – dompurify: DOMPurify: Cross-Site Scripting vulnerability allows arbitrary code execution
items.description: DOMPurify before 3.3.2 contains a mutation-XSS vulnerability when sanitized HTML is reinserted into special parsing contexts using innerHTML with wrappers like script, xmp, iframe, noembed, noframes, or noscript. Attackers can craft payloads with closing sequences that break out of the wrapper context during reparsing, reactivating dangerous markup with event handlers to execute JavaScript.

items.title: dompurify 2.5.9 – DOMPurify: IN_PLACE hook removal leaves a detached subtree executable, causing XSS

During `IN_PLACE` sanitization, a hook that removes an element can leave that element's detached descendants executable. A descendant image can retain its attacker-provided `onload` handler and fire after `sanitize()` returns, even though the returned root is clean and the image remains disconnected from the document.

### Details

In DOMPurify 3.4.12, `_sanitizeElements()` in `src/purify.ts:1862-1904` runs the `beforeSanitizeElements` or `uponSanitizeElement` hook and returns immediately when the hook detached the current node. The return does not call `_neutralizeSubtree(current

items.title: dompurify 2.5.9 – dompurify: DOMPurify: Client-side arbitrary code execution due to improper Trusted Types policy reset
items.description: DOMPurify 3.0.0 before 3.4.9 does not reset the retained Trusted Types policy when clearConfig() is called, so a DOMPurify instance reused across trust boundaries stays bound to a previously supplied TRUSTED_TYPES_POLICY. A later caller that requests RETURN_TRUSTED_TYPE output receives a TrustedHTML object created by the old (potentially unsafe) policy rather than a clean default, which can lead to script execution at a Trusted Types sink. Passing TRUSTED_TYPES_POLICY: null on the later call also does not clear the retained policy.

items.title: dompurify 2.5.9 – dompurify: DOMPurify: Cross-site scripting vulnerability via attacker-controlled nodeName
items.description: DOMPurify through 3.4.6 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability in IN_PLACE mode that trusts attacker-controlled nodeName on live non-form nodes. Attackers can supply hostile live DOM objects with real script children whose observable nodeName is clobbered to appear as allowed elements, causing scripts to execute when the sanitized tree is inserted into a live document.

items.title: dompurify 2.5.9 – dompurify: DOMPurify: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via custom element attribute bypass
items.description: DOMPurify before 3.4.12 fails to execute afterSanitizeElements hook for custom elements allowed via CUSTOM_ELEMENT_HANDLING.tagNameCheck, allowing attributes to bypass application security policies. Attackers can preserve sensitive attributes on custom elements that later re-inject them into innerHTML sinks, creating second-order XSS gadgets.

items.title: fflate 0.8.2 – fflate: fflate: Denial of Service via crafted ZIP archives
items.description: fflate through 0.8.2 is vulnerable to denial of service via an infinite loop in unzipSync(). A crafted ZIP archive with a central directory entry declaring compressed_size=0xFFFFFFFF (ZIP64 sentinel) but missing the required ZIP64 extra field tag 0x0001 causes z64e() to loop indefinitely due to out-of-bounds reads returning undefined, which coerces to 0, keeping the loop condition permanently true.

items.title: jspdf 2.5.2 – jspdf: jsPDF Local File Inclusion/Path Traversal vulnerability
items.description: jsPDF is a library to generate PDFs in JavaScript. Prior to version 4.0.0, user control of the first argument of the loadFile method in the node.js build allows local file inclusion/path traversal. If given the possibility to pass unsanitized paths to the loadFile method, a user can retrieve file contents of arbitrary files in the local file system the node process is running in. The file contents are included verbatim in the generated PDFs. Other affected methods are `addImage`, `html`, and `addFont`. Only the node.js builds of the library are affected, namely the `dist/jspdf.node.js` and `di

triage.explanation: This is only exploitable if the application uses jsPDF's Node.js build and passes user-controlled paths into loadFile. In a typical browser React app, that code path is often unreachable, but if server-side PDF generation exists it could expose local file reads.
triage.fix: Verify whether jsPDF is used in Node/server-side code and whether loadFile is called with untrusted input. If yes, upgrade jspdf to >=4.0.0 and restrict file access to an allowlisted directory or remove user-controlled file paths entirely.

items.title: jspdf 2.5.2 – jspdf: jsPDF: Cross site scripting via unsanitized output options
items.description: jsPDF is a library to generate PDFs in JavaScript. Prior to version 4.2.1, user control of the `options` argument of the `output` function allows attackers to inject arbitrary HTML (such as scripts) into the browser context the created PDF is opened in. The vulnerability can be exploited in the following scenario: the attacker provides values for the output options, for example via a web interface. These values are then passed unsanitized (automatically or semi-automatically) to the attack victim. The victim creates and opens a PDF with the attack vector using one of the vulnerable method over

triage.explanation: The issue matters only if the app lets attackers influence jsPDF output() options and then opens the generated PDF/HTML in a browser context. If jsPDF is used only with fixed options or only for download blobs, impact may be limited.
triage.fix: Audit all calls to output() for user-controlled options, especially html/dataurl-style outputs. Upgrade jspdf to >=4.2.1 and enforce a strict allowlist of output modes instead of passing arbitrary options.

items.title: jspdf 2.5.2 – jsPDF Bypass Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS)
items.description: jsPDF is a library to generate PDFs in JavaScript. Prior to 3.0.1, user control of the first argument of the addImage method results in CPU utilization and denial of service. If given the possibility to pass unsanitised image urls to the addImage method, a user can provide a harmful data-url that results in high CPU utilization and denial of service. Other affected methods are html and addSvgAsImage. The vulnerability was fixed in jsPDF 3.0.1.

triage.explanation: If the app accepts user-supplied image URLs/data and feeds them to addImage, an attacker can trigger excessive CPU usage in the client or server during PDF generation. This is a common pattern in PDF features that embed uploaded or remote images.
triage.fix: Upgrade jspdf to >=3.0.1. Additionally, validate image sources, reject data URLs from untrusted users, cap input size, and preprocess images with a hardened image library before passing them to jsPDF.

items.title: jspdf 2.5.2 – jspdf: jsPDF Denial of Service (DoS)
items.description: jsPDF is a library to generate PDFs in JavaScript. Prior to 3.0.2, user control of the first argument of the addImage method results in CPU utilization and denial of service. If given the possibility to pass unsanitized image data or URLs to the addImage method, a user can provide a harmful PNG file that results in high CPU utilization and denial of service. The vulnerability was fixed in jsPDF 3.0.2.

triage.explanation: This DoS affects addImage handling of crafted PNG input, which is relevant whenever untrusted images can be embedded into generated PDFs. Even in a browser app, this can freeze the tab; on a server it can exhaust worker resources.
triage.fix: Upgrade jspdf to >=3.0.2. Enforce file size and dimension limits, verify MIME/content signatures, and transcode uploaded PNGs through a trusted image processing step before PDF generation.

items.title: jspdf 2.5.2 – jsPDF: jsPDF: Denial of Service due to excessive memory allocation from crafted BMP images
items.description: jsPDF is a library to generate PDFs in JavaScript. Prior to 4.1.0, user control of the first argument of the addImage method results in denial of service. If given the possibility to pass unsanitized image data or URLs to the addImage method, a user can provide a harmful BMP file that results in out of memory errors and denial of service. Harmful BMP files have large width and/or height entries in their headers, which lead to excessive memory allocation. The html method is also affected. The vulnerability has been fixed in jsPDF@4.1.0.

triage.explanation: Crafted BMP images can cause excessive memory allocation through addImage, so any feature that inserts user-controlled images into PDFs is exposed to denial of service. The risk is higher for backend PDF generation services but still relevant client-side.
triage.fix: Upgrade jspdf to >=4.1.0. Block BMP input from untrusted sources or normalize all images to safe formats with bounded dimensions before calling addImage.

items.title: jspdf 2.5.2 – jsPDF: jsPDF: Arbitrary code execution via unsanitized input in Acroform module
items.description: jsPDF is a library to generate PDFs in JavaScript. Prior to 4.1.0, user control of properties and methods of the Acroform module allows users to inject arbitrary PDF objects, such as JavaScript actions. If given the possibility to pass unsanitized input to one of the following methods or properties, a user can inject arbitrary PDF objects, such as JavaScript actions, which are executed when the victim opens the document. items.title: c-ares 1.34.5-r0 – c-ares: c-ares: Use-after-free / double-free in query-completion handling
items.description: c-ares is an asynchronous resolver library. From ver 1.32.3 until 1.34.7, a use-after-free / double-free in c-ares' query-completion handling. The same flaw — a query's callback being invoked while the query is still linked in the channel's internal lookup structures — is present at multiple points in the resend/finish path (timeout handling, response handling, and query dispatch). If the query, or for ares_getaddrinfo() the owning host_query, is freed as a side effect of that callback, it is then accessed and/or freed a second time. This vulnerability is fixed in ver 1.34.7.

items.title: c-ares 1.34.5-r0 – c-ares: c-ares: Denial of Service due to query termination after maximum attempts
items.description: c-ares is an asynchronous resolver library. Versions 1.32.3 through 1.34.5  terminate a query after maximum attempts when using read_answer() and process_answer(), which can cause a Denial of Service. This issue is fixed in version 1.34.6.

items.title: curl 8.12.1-r1 – libcurl: curl: QUIC certificate check skip with wolfSSL
items.description: libcurl accidentally skips the certificate verification for QUIC connections when connecting to a host specified as an IP address in the URL. Therefore, it does not detect impostors or man-in-the-middle attacks.

items.title: curl 8.12.1-r1 – curl: libcurl: QUIC Certificate Pinning Bypass
items.description: libcurl supports *pinning* of the server certificate public key for HTTPS transfers. Due to an omission, this check is not performed when connecting with QUIC for HTTP/3, when the TLS backend is wolfSSL. Documentation says the option works with wolfSSL, failing to specify that it does not for QUIC and HTTP/3. Since pinning makes the transfer succeed if the pin is fine, users could unwittingly connect to an impostor server without noticing.

items.title: curl 8.12.1-r1 – curl: libcurl: WebSocket endless loop
items.description:
Due to a mistake in libcurl's WebSocket code, a malicious server can send a
particularly crafted packet which makes libcurl get trapped in an endless
busy-loop.

There is no other way for the application to escape or exit this loop other
than killing the thread/process.

This might be used to DoS libcurl-using application.

items.title: curl 8.12.1-r1 – curl: predictable WebSocket mask
items.description:
curl's WebSocket code did not update the 32-bit mask pattern for each new
outgoing frame as the specification says. Instead it used a fixed mask that
persisted and was used throughout the entire connection.

A predictable mask pattern allows for a malicious server to induce traffic
between the two communicating parties that could be interpreted by an involved
proxy (configured or transparent) as genuine, real, HTTP traffic with content
and thereby poison its cache. That cached poisoned content could then be
served to all users of that proxy.

items.title: libcurl 8.12.1-r1 – libcurl: curl: QUIC certificate check skip with wolfSSL
items.description: libcurl accidentally skips the certificate verification for QUIC connections when connecting to a host specified as an IP address in the URL. Therefore, it does not detect impostors or man-in-the-middle attacks.

items.title: libcurl 8.12.1-r1 – curl: libcurl: QUIC Certificate Pinning Bypass
items.description: libcurl supports *pinning* of the server certificate public key for HTTPS transfers. Due to an omission, this check is not performed when connecting with QUIC for HTTP/3, when the TLS backend is wolfSSL. Documentation says the option works with wolfSSL, failing to specify that it does not for QUIC and HTTP/3. Since pinning makes the transfer succeed if the pin is fine, users could unwittingly connect to an impostor server without noticing.

items.title: libcurl 8.12.1-r1 – curl: libcurl: WebSocket endless loop
items.description:
Due to a mistake in libcurl's WebSocket code, a malicious server can send a
particularly crafted packet which makes libcurl get trapped in an endless
busy-loop.

There is no other way for the application to escape or exit this loop other
than killing the thread/process.

This might be used to DoS libcurl-using application.

2. curl is redirected to or otherwise made to speak with `http://target` (same
   hostname, but using clear text HTTP) using the same cookie set
3. The same cookie name is set - but with only a slash as path (`path="/"`).
   Since this site is not secure, the cookie *should* be ignored.
4. A bug in the path comparison logic makes curl read outside a heap buffer

items.title: libcurl 8.12.1-r1 – curl: predictable WebSocket mask
items.description:
curl's WebSocket code did not update the 32-bit mask pattern for each new
outgoing frame as the specification says. Instead it used a fixed mask that
persisted and was used throughout the entire connection.

A predictable mask pattern allows for a malicious server to induce traffic
between the two communicating parties that could be interpreted by an involved
proxy (configured or transparent) as genuine, real, HTTP traffic with content
and thereby poison its cache. That cached poisoned content could then be
served to all users of that proxy.

items.description: LIBPNG is a reference library for use in applications that read, create, and manipulate PNG (Portable Network Graphics) raster image files. From version 1.6.0 to before 1.6.51, an out-of-bounds read vulnerability exists in png_image_read_composite when processing palette images with PNG_FLAG_OPTIMIZE_ALPHA enabled. The palette compositing code in png_init_read_transformations incorrectly applies background compositing during premultiplication, violating the invariant component ≤ alpha × 257 required by the simplified PNG API. This issue has been patched in version 1.6.51.

Attacker-crafted interlaced PNG files cause heap writes beyond allocated buffer bounds. This issue has been patched in version 1.6.51.

items.title: libpng 1.6.47-r0 – libpng: LIBPNG out-of-bounds read in png_image_read_composite
items.description: LIBPNG is a reference library for use in applications that read, create, and manipulate PNG (Portable Network Graphics) raster image files. The PNG files that trigger this vulnerability are valid per the PNG specification; the bug is in libpng's internal state management. Upgrade to libpng 1.6.52 or later.

Issue summary: A specially crafted password-encrypted CMS message
can trigger a NULL pointer dereference during CMS decryption.

Impact summary: This NULL pointer dereference leads to an application crash
and a Denial of Service.

The CMS PasswordRecipientInfo.keyDerivationAlgorithm field is defined as
OPTIONAL in the ASN.1 specification and may therefore be absent in specially
crafted inputs. During the password-based CMS decryption the OpenSSL
CMS implementation dereferences this field without first checking whether it
was present.

items.description:

victim's private RSA key.

items.description:
Issue summary: When EVP_PKEY_derive_set_peer() is called with a DHX (X9.42)
peer key, the peer key is not properly checked for the subgroup membership.

victim's p and g parameters, a forged q = r (a small prime factor of the
cofactor (p−1)/q_local), and a public value Y of order r can recover the
victim's private key after a small number of key exchange attempts.

items.description:

items.description:

items.title: libxml2 2.13.4-r6 – libxml: Heap use after free (UAF) leads to Denial of service (DoS)
items.description: A use-after-free vulnerability was found in libxml2. This issue occurs when parsing XPath elements under certain circumstances when the XML schematron has the <sch:name path="..."/> schema elements. This flaw allows a malicious actor to craft a malicious XML document used as input for libxml, resulting in the program's crash using libxml or other possible undefined behaviors.

items.title: libxml2 2.13.4-r6 – libxml: Null pointer dereference leads to Denial of service (DoS)
items.description: A NULL pointer dereference vulnerability was found in libxml2 when processing XPath XML expressions. This flaw allows an attacker to craft a malicious XML input to libxml2, leading to a denial of service.

items.title: libxml2 2.13.4-r6 – libxml: Type confusion leads to Denial of service (DoS)
items.description: A vulnerability was found in libxml2. Processing certain sch:name elements from the input XML file can trigger a memory corruption issue. This flaw allows an attacker to craft a malicious XML input file that can lead libxml to crash, resulting in a denial of service or other possible undefined behavior due to sensitive data being corrupted in memory.

items.title: libxml2 2.13.4-r6 – libxml2: libxml2: Denial of Service via crafted XSD-validated document
items.description: A flaw was found in libxml2. This vulnerability occurs when the library processes a specially crafted XML Schema Definition (XSD) validated document that includes an internal entity reference. An attacker could exploit this by providing a malicious document, leading to a type confusion error that causes the application to crash. This results in a denial of service (DoS), making the affected system or application unavailable.

items.title: libxml2 2.13.4-r6 – libxml2: Integer Overflow in xmlBuildQName() Leads to Stack Buffer Overflow in libxml2
items.description: A flaw was found in libxml2's xmlBuildQName function, where integer overflows in buffer size calculations can lead to a stack-based buffer overflow. This issue can result in memory corruption or a denial of service when processing crafted input.

items.title: libxml2 2.13.4-r6 – libxml2: Stack Buffer Overflow in xmllint Interactive Shell Command Handling
items.description: A flaw was found in the interactive shell of the xmllint command-line tool, used for parsing XML files. When a user inputs an overly long command, the program does not check the input size properly, which can cause it to crash. This issue might allow attackers to run harmful code in rare configurations without modern protections.

items.title: libxpm 3.5.17-r0 – libXpm: libXpm: Denial of Service via out-of-bounds read in XPM file parsing
items.description: A flaw was found in libXpm. A local user with low privileges could exploit an Out-of-Bounds Read vulnerability in the `xpmNextWord()` function by processing a specially crafted or very small XPM (X PixMap) image file. This improper validation of file boundaries can cause an internal pointer to read beyond the file's end, leading to application crashes and Denial of Service conditions.

items.title: musl 1.2.5-r9 – musl: musl libc: Arbitrary code execution and denial of service via stack-based memory corruption in qsort
items.description: An issue was discovered in musl libc 0.7.10 through 1.2.6. Stack-based memory corruption can occur during qsort of very large arrays, due to incorrectly implemented double-word primitives. The number of elements must exceed about seven million, i.e., the 32nd Leonardo number on 32-bit platforms (or the 64th Leonardo number on 64-bit platforms, which is not practical).

items.title: musl 1.2.5-r9 – musl libc: GB18030 4-byte Decoder: musl libc: Denial of Service via inefficient algorithmic complexity in iconv
items.description: A security flaw has been discovered in musl libc up to 1.2.6. Affected is the function iconv of the file src/locale/iconv.c of the component GB18030 4-byte Decoder. Performing a manipulation results in inefficient algorithmic complexity. The attack must be initiated from a local position. To fix this issue, it is recommended to deploy a patch.

items.title: tiff 4.7.0-r0 – libtiff: libtiff: Arbitrary code execution or denial of service via signed integer overflow in TIFF file processing
items.description: A flaw was found in the libtiff library. A remote attacker could exploit a signed integer overflow vulnerability in the putcontig8bitYCbCr44tile function by providing a specially crafted TIFF file. This flaw can lead to an out-of-bounds heap write due to incorrect memory pointer calculations, potentially causing a denial of service (application crash) or arbitrary code execution.

items.title: tiff 4.7.0-r0 – libtiff: LibTIFF memory corruption
items.description: A weakness has been identified in LibTIFF 4.7.0. This affects the function main of the file tiffcrop.c of the component tiffcrop. Executing manipulation can lead to memory corruption. The attack can only be executed locally. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be exploited.

items.title: xz-libs 5.6.3-r1 – xz: XZ Utils: Denial of Service via buffer overflow in index decoding
items.description: XZ Utils provide a general-purpose data-compression library plus command-line tools. Prior to version 5.8.3, if lzma_index_decoder() was used to decode an Index that contained no Records, the resulting lzma_index was left in a state where where a subsequent lzma_index_append() would allocate too little memory, and a buffer overflow would occur. This issue has been patched in version 5.8.3.

items.title: zlib 1.3.1-r2 – zlib: zlib: Arbitrary code execution via buffer overflow in untgz utility
items.description: zlib versions up to and including 1.3.1.2 include a global buffer overflow in the untgz utility located under contrib/untgz. The vulnerability is limited to the standalone demonstration utility and does not affect the core zlib compression library. The flaw occurs when a user executes the untgz command with an excessively long archive name supplied via the command line, leading to an out-of-bounds write in a fixed-size global buffer.

items.title: zlib 1.3.1-r2 – zlib: zlib: Denial of Service via infinite loop in CRC32 combine functions
items.description: zlib before 1.3.2 allows CPU consumption via crc32_combine64 and crc32_combine_gen64 because x2nmodp can do right shifts within a loop that has no termination condition.

items.title: zlib 1.3.1-r2 – zlib versions 1.3.1.2 through 1.3.2 contain a heap buffer overflow vul ...
items.description: zlib versions 1.3.1.2 through 1.3.2 contain a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in the gz_vacate() function when processing non-blocking gzwrite() operations with stale external buffer pointers. Attackers can trigger the overflow by calling gzprintf() or gzvprintf() after a write stall, causing an unchecked memmove() to write beyond the internal input buffer boundary.

it('debounce only invokes the latest call and supports cancellation', async () => {
    const calls = []
    const debounced = debounce((value) => calls.push(value), 20)

    debounced('first')
    debounced('second')
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 35))

    expect(calls).toEqual(['second'])

    debounced('third')
    debounced.cancel()
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 35))

    expect(calls).toEqual(['second'])
  })

items.why: It passed because the application ignored the earlier call, kept the latest one, and successfully cancelled the pending final call.

items.description: A flaw was found in util-linux. When an /etc/fstab entry uses the user option together with X-mount.owner, X-mount.group, or X-mount.mode, mount(8) changes ownership or permissions on the mount target after mounting without re-verifying the path. A local unprivileged user can exploit this Time-of-Check-Time-of-Use (TOCTOU) window by swapping the target directory, redirecting the ownership/permission change to an arbitrary file and potentially escalating privileges to root.

items.title: bsdutils 1:2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: TOCTOU in the mount program via ancestor directory swap on target path
items.description: When an /etc/fstab entry is configured with the user or users option, mount(8) validates the target path before performing the mount syscall, creating a Time-of-Check-Time-of-Use (TOCTOU) window. A local unprivileged user with write access to an ancestor directory of the mount target can swap that directory to redirect the mount to an arbitrary root-owned location, potentially escalating privileges to root.

items.title: bsdutils 1:2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: SUID mount(8) allows nosuid/noexec bypass via LIBMOUNT_FORCE_MOUNT2
items.description: A flaw was found in util-linux. The mount(8) SUID binary does not sanitize the LIBMOUNT_FORCE_MOUNT2 environment variable before use. A local unprivileged user can set this variable to force mount(8) to use the legacy two-step mount(2) code path, which applies security restrictions such as nosuid and noexec after the mount is already active. During this window, an attacker can execute a SUID binary from the mounted filesystem, allowing local privilege escalation to root.

items.title: bsdutils 1:2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: failed external mount helper still runs privileged X-mount post-hooks
items.description: util-linux versions through 2.41.5 and 2.42.2 fail to check mount helper exit status before running post-mount hooks, allowing unprivileged users to execute privileged operations on pre-existing filesystems. Attackers can exploit X-mount.idmap or X-mount.owner hooks to clone filesystems with inherited suid bits or modify target inode permissions after a helper fails, achieving privilege escalation.

items.title: bsdutils 1:2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: nsenter --join-cgroup leaks root cgroup migration authority
items.description: The nsenter --join-cgroup option opens the target cgroup.procs file as root and leaves that file descriptor open across later namespace and credential changes and across execve(). Because the kernel checks later cgroup migrations using the credentials from the original open, a program run in an attacker-controlled target can inherit root's ability to move host processes between cgroups. After a privileged operator uses --join-cgroup against that target, an unprivileged user can migrate and terminate unrelated root processes.

items.title: bsdutils 1:2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: X-mount.subdir detached-tree resolution can escape via intermediate symlinks
items.description: The X-mount.subdir option uses a detached-tree fast path on Linux 6.15 and later and passes the configured subdirectory to open_tree() with AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW. That flag does not stop intermediate symlink traversal or keep resolution inside the newly mounted filesystem. A local unprivileged user with an fstab-authorized X-mount.subdir entry can attach a host path at the intended mountpoint.

items.title: bsdutils 1:2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: restricted bind mounts do not pin the source, allowing X-mount.owner/group/mode redirection
items.description: A flaw was found in util-linux. Restricted bind mounts take the source path from fstab but do not pin that source before the privileged mount. A local unprivileged user who can replace the authorized source or a writable ancestor can redirect SUID mount(8) to bind another host directory. If the fstab entry also sets X-mount.owner, X-mount.group, or X-mount.mode, root then changes ownership or mode on that redirected inode.

items.title: libblkid1 2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: TOCTOU in the mount program when applying post-mount ownership/mode changes
items.description: A flaw was found in util-linux. When an /etc/fstab entry uses the user option together with X-mount.owner, X-mount.group, or X-mount.mode, mount(8) changes ownership or permissions on the mount target after mounting without re-verifying the path. A local unprivileged user can exploit this Time-of-Check-Time-of-Use (TOCTOU) window by swapping the target directory, redirecting the ownership/permission change to an arbitrary file and potentially escalating privileges to root.

items.title: libblkid1 2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: TOCTOU in the mount program via ancestor directory swap on target path
items.description: When an /etc/fstab entry is configured with the user or users option, mount(8) validates the target path before performing the mount syscall, creating a Time-of-Check-Time-of-Use (TOCTOU) window. A local unprivileged user with write access to an ancestor directory of the mount target can swap that directory to redirect the mount to an arbitrary root-owned location, potentially escalating privileges to root.

items.title: libblkid1 2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: SUID mount(8) allows nosuid/noexec bypass via LIBMOUNT_FORCE_MOUNT2
items.description: A flaw was found in util-linux. The mount(8) SUID binary does not sanitize the LIBMOUNT_FORCE_MOUNT2 environment variable before use. A local unprivileged user can set this variable to force mount(8) to use the legacy two-step mount(2) code path, which applies security restrictions such as nosuid and noexec after the mount is already active. During this window, an attacker can execute a SUID binary from the mounted filesystem, allowing local privilege escalation to root.

items.title: libblkid1 2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: failed external mount helper still runs privileged X-mount post-hooks
items.description: util-linux versions through 2.41.5 and 2.42.2 fail to check mount helper exit status before running post-mount hooks, allowing unprivileged users to execute privileged operations on pre-existing filesystems. Attackers can exploit X-mount.idmap or X-mount.owner hooks to clone filesystems with inherited suid bits or modify target inode permissions after a helper fails, achieving privilege escalation.

items.title: libblkid1 2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: nsenter --join-cgroup leaks root cgroup migration authority
items.description: The nsenter --join-cgroup option opens the target cgroup.procs file as root and leaves that file descriptor open across later namespace and credential changes and across execve(). Because the kernel checks later cgroup migrations using the credentials from the original open, a program run in an attacker-controlled target can inherit root's ability to move host processes between cgroups. After a privileged operator uses --join-cgroup against that target, an unprivileged user can migrate and terminate unrelated root processes.

items.title: libblkid1 2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: X-mount.subdir detached-tree resolution can escape via intermediate symlinks
items.description: The X-mount.subdir option uses a detached-tree fast path on Linux 6.15 and later and passes the configured subdirectory to open_tree() with AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW. That flag does not stop intermediate symlink traversal or keep resolution inside the newly mounted filesystem. A local unprivileged user with an fstab-authorized X-mount.subdir entry can attach a host path at the intended mountpoint.

items.title: libblkid1 2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: restricted bind mounts do not pin the source, allowing X-mount.owner/group/mode redirection
items.description: A flaw was found in util-linux. Restricted bind mounts take the source path from fstab but do not pin that source before the privileged mount. A local unprivileged user who can replace the authorized source or a writable ancestor can redirect SUID mount(8) to bind another host directory. If the fstab entry also sets X-mount.owner, X-mount.group, or X-mount.mode, root then changes ownership or mode on that redirected inode.

items.title: libc-bin 2.41-12 – glibc: glibc: Denial of Service via out-of-bounds read in strncasecmp
items.description:
The strncasecmp function in the GNU C Library 2.24 and later optimized for the Power8 architecture may read one byte beyond the input size limit, which may crash a program when that byte is not readable.

This condition may happen when the input strings to the strncasecmp function are attacker controlled in an application and they match all the way up to the edge of their page and the neighbouring page is either not mapped or is not readable.

items.title: libc6 2.41-12 – glibc: glibc: Information disclosure via zero-valued network query

items.title: libc6 2.41-12 – glibc: glibc: Heap buffer overflow via attacker-controlled fopen mode string
items.description:
Passing an effectively empty string to the `,ccs=` syntax extension of the mode argument in the `fopen` function in the GNU C Library version 2.45 or earlier may result in a heap buffer overflow when the mode string input to the function is attacker controlled.



This usage pattern is not seen in applications in common GNU/Linux distributions and applications that process user-supplied values for `ccs` should not pass them through without validation.

items.title: libc6 2.41-12 – glibc: Buffer Overflow in strfmon right-justification padding
items.description:
Calling strfmon and strfmon_l in the GNU C Library version 2.38 to 2.44 can write past the end of the caller-supplied output buffer when a conversion uses right-justified width padding.

Exploitation requires an application code path that calls strfmon or strfmon_l with right-justified width padding into a destination buffer that is large enough for the padding to succeed but too small for the internal memmove call. The field width or format may be attacker-influenced or a fixed susceptible pattern in the caller.

At the time of publication, no network-facing application impact is known.

items.title: libc6 2.41-12 – glibc: glibc: Denial of Service via iconv() function with specific character sets
items.description:
The iconv() function in the GNU C Library versions 2.43 and earlier may crash due to an assertion failure when converting inputs from the IBM1390 or IBM1399 character sets, which may be used to remotely crash an application.



This vulnerability can be trivially mitigated by removing the IBM1390 and IBM1399 character sets from systems that do not need them.

items.title: libc6 2.41-12 – glibc: glibc: Local attacker can cause denial of service and information disclosure via stack-based buffer overflow.
items.description:
A stack-based buffer overflow in the dynamic loader (ld.so) of the GNU C Library (glibc) versions 2.14 through 2.44 allows a local attacker to crash or corrupt the memory of setuid/setgid (AT_SECURE) programs.

When such a program's DT_RPATH or DT_RUNPATH begins with $ORIGIN and is followed by NUL or '/' the loader both reads past the end of the path buffer and writes past the end of a stack-allocated internal buffer. The corrupted loader stack can lead to a loader crash (denial of service) and limited disclosure of process memory.

items.description: The glob implementation in the GNU C Library (aka glibc or libc6) allows remote authenticated users to cause a denial of service (CPU and memory consumption) via crafted glob expressions that do not match any pathnames, as demonstrated by glob expressions in STAT commands to an FTP daemon, a different vulnerability than CVE-2010-2632.

items.title: libcap2 1:2.75-10+b1 – libcap: libcap: Privilege escalation via TOCTOU race condition in cap_set_file()
items.description: A flaw was found in libcap. A local unprivileged user can exploit a Time-of-check-to-time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition in the `cap_set_file()` function. This allows an attacker with write access to a parent directory to redirect file capability updates to an attacker-controlled file. By doing so, capabilities can be injected into or stripped from unintended executables, leading to privilege escalation.

items.title: libgcc-s1 14.2.0-19 – gcc-toolset-15-gcc: gcc: gcc-toolset-16: gcc: Denial of Service via use-after-free in binary heap erase_if
items.description: A flaw was found in GCC. When an application calls the erase_if function on a binary heap priority queue in libstdc++, the library reallocates storage but fails to update its internal entry pointer. An attacker capable of triggering this operation can exploit this use-after-free condition, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) via an application crash or potential memory corruption.

items.title: libgcc-s1 14.2.0-19 – gcc: libstdc++ integer overflow in `new` operator
items.description: A flaw was found in libstdc++. An integer overflow can occur when processing large inputs to the aligned operator new in the C++ library. This vulnerability could lead to an undersized memory allocation, potentially causing memory corruption or application instability.

items.title: liblastlog2-2 2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: TOCTOU in the mount program when applying post-mount ownership/mode changes
items.description: A flaw was found in util-linux. When an /etc/fstab entry uses the user option together with X-mount.owner, X-mount.group, or X-mount.mode, mount(8) changes ownership or permissions on the mount target after mounting without re-verifying the path. A local unprivileged user can exploit this Time-of-Check-Time-of-Use (TOCTOU) window by swapping the target directory, redirecting the ownership/permission change to an arbitrary file and potentially escalating privileges to root.

items.title: liblastlog2-2 2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: TOCTOU in the mount program via ancestor directory swap on target path
items.description: When an /etc/fstab entry is configured with the user or users option, mount(8) validates the target path before performing the mount syscall, creating a Time-of-Check-Time-of-Use (TOCTOU) window. A local unprivileged user with write access to an ancestor directory of the mount target can swap that directory to redirect the mount to an arbitrary root-owned location, potentially escalating privileges to root.

items.title: liblastlog2-2 2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: SUID mount(8) allows nosuid/noexec bypass via LIBMOUNT_FORCE_MOUNT2
items.description: A flaw was found in util-linux. The mount(8) SUID binary does not sanitize the LIBMOUNT_FORCE_MOUNT2 environment variable before use. A local unprivileged user can set this variable to force mount(8) to use the legacy two-step mount(2) code path, which applies security restrictions such as nosuid and noexec after the mount is already active. During this window, an attacker can execute a SUID binary from the mounted filesystem, allowing local privilege escalation to root.

items.title: liblastlog2-2 2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: failed external mount helper still runs privileged X-mount post-hooks
items.description: util-linux versions through 2.41.5 and 2.42.2 fail to check mount helper exit status before running post-mount hooks, allowing unprivileged users to execute privileged operations on pre-existing filesystems. Attackers can exploit X-mount.idmap or X-mount.owner hooks to clone filesystems with inherited suid bits or modify target inode permissions after a helper fails, achieving privilege escalation.

items.title: liblastlog2-2 2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: nsenter --join-cgroup leaks root cgroup migration authority
items.description: The nsenter --join-cgroup option opens the target cgroup.procs file as root and leaves that file descriptor open across later namespace and credential changes and across execve(). Because the kernel checks later cgroup migrations using the credentials from the original open, a program run in an attacker-controlled target can inherit root's ability to move host processes between cgroups. After a privileged operator uses --join-cgroup against that target, an unprivileged user can migrate and terminate unrelated root processes.

items.title: liblastlog2-2 2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: X-mount.subdir detached-tree resolution can escape via intermediate symlinks
items.description: The X-mount.subdir option uses a detached-tree fast path on Linux 6.15 and later and passes the configured subdirectory to open_tree() with AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW. That flag does not stop intermediate symlink traversal or keep resolution inside the newly mounted filesystem. A local unprivileged user with an fstab-authorized X-mount.subdir entry can attach a host path at the intended mountpoint.

items.title: liblastlog2-2 2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: restricted bind mounts do not pin the source, allowing X-mount.owner/group/mode redirection
items.description: A flaw was found in util-linux. Restricted bind mounts take the source path from fstab but do not pin that source before the privileged mount. A local unprivileged user who can replace the authorized source or a writable ancestor can redirect SUID mount(8) to bind another host directory. If the fstab entry also sets X-mount.owner, X-mount.group, or X-mount.mode, root then changes ownership or mode on that redirected inode.

items.title: liblastlog2-2 2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: heap use-after-free in libblkid nested partition probing
items.description: A flaw was found in the libblkid library of util-linux. During nested partition probing, the BSD, Minix, Solaris x86, and UnixWare partition probers cache a raw pointer to a parent partition entry in a dynamically allocated array. When subsequent partition additions cause the array to be reallocated, this pointer becomes stale, leading to a heap use-after-free read. items.description: util-linux is a random collection of Linux utilities.
