items.title: fast-uri 3.1.3 – fast-uri: Fast-uri: Security policy bypass due to URL parsing inconsistency
items.description: Impact: fast-uri versions from 2.3.1 through 4.1.0 (including the 3.x line up to 3.1.3 and the 2.x line up to 2.4.2) do not treat a literal backslash character (U+005C) as an authority delimiter. Node's native WHATWG URL parser, used by fetch, undici, and Node's http and https clients, normalizes the backslash to a forward slash for special schemes such as http, https, ws, wss, ftp, and file. As a result, the two parsers extract different hosts from the same input string. Applications that use fast-uri to enforce host-based policy such as allowlists, denylists, loopback or SSRF filtering, redi

triage.explanation: The fast-uri parser inconsistencies are real, but they matter only if this application uses fast-uri for security decisions such as SSRF allow/deny logic, redirect validation, webhook URL validation, or host policy enforcement. If fast-uri is only a transitive helper not used on attacker-controlled URLs, practical impact may be low.
triage.fix: Upgrade fast-uri to at least 3.1.5/4.1.2 or later patched versions, and review any code that validates or normalizes untrusted URLs before passing them to Node/undici/fetch/http clients.

items.title: fast-uri 3.1.3 – fast-uri: fast-uri: Host confusion vulnerability via backslash in URI authority
items.description: fast-uri before 4.1.2, 3.1.5, and 2.4.4 requires a literal double forward slash to recognize a URI authority, so a reference that uses a backslash based introducer in place of it (backslash backslash, forward slash backslash, or backslash forward slash) is parsed with no authority and folds into the path. Node's native WHATWG URL parser instead treats a backslash as interchangeable with a forward slash for special schemes, so the two parsers extract different hosts from the same input. Applications that use fast-uri to enforce host based policy such as allowlists, SSRF filtering, or redirect v

triage.explanation: Host confusion via backslash authority parsing can bypass URL validation when one parser is used for checks and another for network access. This is important if the app accepts user-supplied URLs and relies on fast-uri normalization or parsing for access control.
triage.fix: Upgrade fast-uri to at least 3.1.5 or 4.1.2, and standardize on a single hardened URL parser for both validation and request execution.

items.title: fast-uri 3.1.3 – fast-uri: fast-uri: Server-Side Request Forgery via repeated hostname percent-decoding
items.description: fast-uri is a URI parser for Node.js. It decodes percent escapes in a hostname during parsing and then decodes the parsed hostname a second time during authority recomposition, so a single call to normalize or resolve can turn nested percent-encoded input into a different network destination such as a loopback hostname or address. For example, a doubly encoded host that spells out a loopback name decodes to that live host in one operation, which contradicts RFC 3986 section 2.4 that an implementation must not decode the same string more than once. triage.explanation: Repeated hostname percent-decoding can enable SSRF if normalized output is later fetched or compared against an allowlist. The issue is significant only where attacker-controlled URLs are accepted and fast-uri output influences outbound connections or redirects.
triage.fix: Upgrade fast-uri to a patched release, and reject doubly encoded or ambiguous hostnames while using the same parser semantics for validation and transport.

items.title: fast-uri 3.1.3 – fast-uri: fast-uri: Host confusion via skipped IDN canonicalization
items.description: fast-uri is a URI parser for Node.js. It canonicalizes a host to its ASCII form only when the input carries an explicit scheme, so a scheme-relative reference such as a host preceded by two slashes is returned with its host verbatim and no error set. As a result fast-uri's own entry points disagree with each other: parse, resolve, normalize, and equal can yield different hosts for the same input depending only on whether a scheme is written out, and equal can return opposite verdicts for the same pair of hosts. triage.explanation: Skipped IDN canonicalization can create parser disagreement and host allowlist bypasses for scheme-relative URLs. This matters if the application validates internationalized or scheme-relative user URLs before redirecting or making server-side requests.
triage.fix: Upgrade fast-uri to a patched version and normalize hosts to ASCII/Punycode consistently before any policy checks or outbound use.

items.title: fast-uri 3.1.3 – fast-uri: fast-uri: Server-side request forgery via malformed IPv6 normalization
items.description: fast-uri is a URI parser for Node.js. Its custom parser for bracketed IPv6 literals does not validate the complete IPv6 grammar, so invalid trailing text in an authority can be silently discarded and a malformed attacker-controlled host is turned into a different valid IPv6 destination. For example, a bracketed literal with invalid trailing characters is normalized to the unspecified address, which a Node HTTP client then connects to a local service over loopback, and other malformed literals collapse to private-range addresses. triage.explanation: Malformed IPv6 normalization can turn attacker input into a different destination, which is relevant for SSRF protections and redirect validation. If the app never accepts untrusted URLs or does not use fast-uri in those flows, exploitability is limited.
triage.fix: Upgrade fast-uri to a patched version and add strict URL validation that rejects malformed IPv6 authorities before normalization or connection attempts.

items.title: fast-uri 3.1.3 – fast-uri: fast-uri: URI parsing flaw enables server-side request forgery and redirects
items.description: fast-uri is a URI parser for Node.js. During parsing it runs a legacy decoding pass over the scheme component and never re-escapes the result, and serialization writes the scheme back out verbatim, unlike the host component which is re-escaped. As a result an input whose scheme carries percent-encoded slashes parses as a scheme with no authority, so the parsed host and error are both undefined, yet resolving or normalizing that same input emits a network-path reference whose authority is attacker-chosen and re-parses to that host. triage.explanation: Scheme decoding/serialization flaws can alter the effective URL and enable SSRF or open redirect behavior when untrusted URLs are normalized then reused. This is a real parser bug, but application impact depends on whether fast-uri is in a security-sensitive URL handling path.
triage.fix: Upgrade fast-uri to a patched release and review all uses of URL normalization/serialization on attacker-controlled input, especially before redirects or outbound HTTP requests.

items.title: fast-uri 3.1.3 – fast-uri: fast-uri: Authority Injection via Unvalidated Port Serialization
items.description: fast-uri serializes the port component of a URI without validating it. triage.explanation: Unvalidated port serialization can inject authority delimiters and subvert host-based validation, which is dangerous in SSRF and redirect controls. It is only actionable if this application constructs or validates URLs with fast-uri using attacker-influenced port values.
triage.fix: Upgrade fast-uri to at least 3.1.5/4.1.2 or newer, and enforce numeric-only port validation before URL recomposition or policy checks.

FIX: Keep nginx listening on port `5173`, but change startup so the PID file is written to a writable location (`/tmp/nginx/nginx.pid`) and ensure required writable directories exist for the `nginx` user.

--- eqip-quality-platform: self-healing attempt 2 (deploy) ---
The container is starting nginx, but nginx exits immediately because the command line adds a second `pid` directive:

- base image nginx config already defines `pid` in `/etc/nginx/nginx.conf`
- Dockerfile `CMD` adds `-g "pid /tmp/nginx/nginx.pid; daemon off;"`
- nginx treats that as a duplicate and exits with:
  - `"pid" directive is duplicate in /etc/nginx/nginx.conf:6`

The app is otherwise configured to serve on port `5173`, and nginx listens on all interfaces by default with `listen 5173;`, so the main issue is the startup command.

I fixed the Dockerfile by removing the extra `pid` override and keeping nginx in the foreground:

```dockerfile
CMD ["nginx", "-g", "daemon off;"]
```

suggestions:
--- eqip-quality-platform: self-healing attempt 1 (deploy) ---
Updated the Dockerfile so nginx can run as the non-root `nginx` user and still bind on the expected app port `5173` without trying to write its PID file into `/run`.

ROOT CAUSE: The container starts nginx as `USER nginx`, but nginx still tries to create `/run/nginx.pid`, which is not writable for that non-root user. That causes nginx to exit immediately with `open() "/run/nginx.pid" failed (13: Permission denied)`.

FIX: Keep nginx listening on port `5173`, but change startup so the PID file is written to a writable location (`/tmp/nginx/nginx.pid`) and ensure required writable directories exist for the `nginx` user.

items.title: next 15.1.3 – nextjs: Authorization Bypass in Next.js Middleware
items.description: Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. Starting in version 1.11.4 and prior to versions 12.3.5, 13.5.9, 14.2.25, and 15.2.3, it is possible to bypass authorization checks within a Next.js application, if the authorization check occurs in middleware. If patching to a safe version is infeasible, it is recommend that you prevent external user requests which contain the x-middleware-subrequest header from reaching your Next.js application. This vulnerability is fixed in 12.3.5, 13.5.9, 14.2.25, and 15.2.3.

triage.explanation: This affects Next.js 15.1.3 and can allow authz bypass if this application relies on Next middleware for access control. If protected routes or APIs are gated in middleware, this is release-blocking.
triage.fix: Upgrade Next.js to 15.2.3 or later. As an interim mitigation, move authorization checks into the route handler/server action/page/API logic rather than relying solely on middleware.

items.title: next 15.1.3 – next: React Server Components: Pre-authentication remote code execution via unsafe deserialization
items.description: A pre-authentication remote code execution vulnerability exists in React Server Components versions 19.0.0, 19.1.0, 19.1.1, and 19.2.0 including the following packages: react-server-dom-parcel, react-server-dom-turbopack, and react-server-dom-webpack. The vulnerable code unsafely deserializes payloads from HTTP requests to Server Function endpoints.

triage.explanation: The package version is affected, but exploitability depends on whether the app uses App Router/React Server Components and the vulnerable deserialization path is reachable pre-auth. If the frontend is mostly static or Pages Router only, impact may be limited.
triage.fix: Upgrade Next.js/React to versions containing the React Server Components fix. Confirm whether App Router/RSC endpoints are exposed; if so, prioritize patching immediately and restrict public access where possible.

items.title: next 15.1.3 – next: Next.js: Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution on windows-hosted servers
items.description: Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. From 13.4.0 until 15.5.24 and 16.3.3, Next.js applications using Pages Router or App Router without Cache Components on Windows-hosted servers do not consistently escape backslashes in route segments before constructing incremental-cache paths. In packages/next/src/shared/lib/router/utils/escape-path-delimiters.ts and packages/next/src/server/lib/incremental-cache/file-system-cache.ts, a remote request can supply encoded Windows path separators that traverse outside the intended cache root and expose private build data, inc

triage.explanation: This issue is specific to Windows-hosted Next.js servers. If production and build/runtime environments are Linux containers, it is not applicable to this application.
triage.fix: Confirm all deployed Next.js instances run on Linux, then document the environment-based exception. If any Windows hosting exists, upgrade to a fixed Next.js release immediately.

items.title: next 15.1.3 – Next.js: Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution in Image Optimization API when AVIF files are used
items.description:
A vulnerability in the underlying `libheif` library used by `sharp` which Next.js uses for image optimization can lead to remote code execution when AVIF files are optimized.

Until a fix has propagated, optimization of AVIF files is disabled.

triage.explanation: This can be serious only if the application exposes Next.js image optimization for attacker-supplied AVIF images and uses a vulnerable sharp/libheif chain. The finding is plausible for a public image proxy/upload flow but not automatically exploitable in every app.
triage.fix: Upgrade Next.js and sharp to versions with the propagated fix. Until then, disable AVIF optimization and restrict image optimization to trusted domains/formats.

items.title: next 15.1.3 – nextjs: Next.js denial of service
items.description: Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. From versions 15.0.4-canary.51 to before 15.1.8, a cache poisoning bug leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) condition was found in Next.js. This issue does not impact customers hosted on Vercel. Under certain conditions, this issue may allow a HTTP 204 response to be cached for static pages, leading to the 204 response being served to all users attempting to access the page. This issue has been addressed in version 15.1.8.

triage.explanation: The vulnerable Next.js version matches, but this DoS requires the affected caching behavior and self-hosted deployment conditions. It matters if the app is self-hosted and uses the impacted cache path.
triage.fix: Upgrade Next.js to 15.1.8 or later. Also place the app behind rate limiting/CDN protections and review cache configuration.

items.title: next 15.1.3 – next.js: Next.js: Information disclosure due to middleware bypass in Pages Router with i18n
items.description: Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. From 12.2.0 to before 15.5.16 and 16.2.5, Applications using the Pages Router with i18n configured and middleware/proxy-based authorization can allow unauthorized access to protected page data through locale-less /_next/data/<buildId>/<page>.json requests. In affected configurations, middleware does not run for the unprefixed data route, allowing an attacker to retrieve SSR JSON for protected pages without passing the intended authorization checks. This vulnerability is fixed in 15.5.16 and 16.2.5.

triage.explanation: This only applies if the app uses the Pages Router with i18n plus middleware/proxy-based authorization. If the frontend uses App Router or no i18n, this is likely not applicable.
triage.fix: Verify router mode and i18n usage. If applicable, upgrade Next.js to a fixed version and enforce authorization in page/data handlers, not only middleware.

items.title: next 15.1.3 – Next.js: Next.js: Server-Side Request Forgery via crafted WebSocket upgrade requests
items.description: Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. From 13.4.13 to before 15.5.16 and 16.2.5, self-hosted applications using the built-in Node.js server can be vulnerable to server-side request forgery through crafted WebSocket upgrade requests. An attacker can cause the server to proxy requests to arbitrary internal or external destinations, which may expose internal services or cloud metadata endpoints. Vercel-hosted deployments are not affected. This vulnerability is fixed in 15.5.16 and 16.2.5.

triage.explanation: This SSRF requires self-hosting on the built-in Node.js server and exposure of crafted WebSocket upgrade handling. It is relevant if the app is not behind a platform that terminates or filters such traffic.

items.title: next 15.1.3 – next.js: Next.js: Denial of Service via crafted POST requests to server actions
items.description: Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. In affected configurations, a malicious request can trigger a request-body handling deadlock that leaves connections open for an extended period, consuming file descriptors and server capacity until legitimate users are denied service. This vulnerability is fixed in 15.5.16 and 16.2.5.

triage.explanation: The advisory is tied to Partial Prerendering via Cache Components. If this application is on Next 15.1.3 without Cache Components/PPR enabled, the issue is not applicable.
triage.fix: Confirm Cache Components/PPR are disabled and document the exception. If enabled, upgrade Next.js and add request rate/concurrency limits.

triage.fix: Determine whether App Router and Server Actions are used. If yes, upgrade Next.js to a fixed version and add rate limiting/timeouts at the edge or reverse proxy.

A redirects() rule configured this way is vulnerable to an Open Redirect. This issue has been fixed in versions

items.title: next 15.1.3 – next: Next.js: Server-Side Request Forgery via malicious host redirection in Server Actions
items.description: Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. This requires the attacker's request to control Host-associated headers. In some configurations, it's also possible to obtain internal values that weaken middleware/proxy authorization. Applications that use Server Actions are affected when the incoming host header is not fixed to a trusted value.

triage.explanation: This requires use of Server Actions that forward or redirect requests in a way influenced by attacker input. If the app has no such flows, impact is limited.
triage.fix: Audit Server Actions for redirects/forwards using request-derived URLs or hosts. Upgrade Next.js and enforce strict allowlists for outbound destinations.

items.title: next 15.1.3 – Next.js Vulnerable to Denial of Service with Server Components
items.description:
A vulnerability affects certain React Server Components packages for versions 19.x and frameworks that use the affected packages, including Next.js 13.x, 14.x, 15.x, and 16.x using the App Router. The issue is tracked upstream as [CVE-2026-23870](https://github.com/facebook/react/security/advisories/GHSA-rv78-f8rc-xrxh). 

A specially crafted HTTP request can be sent to any App Router Server Function endpoint that, when deserialized, may trigger excessive CPU usage. This can result in denial of service in unpatched environments.

triage.fix: Upgrade to patched Next.js/React versions. Add request size/rate limits and consider WAF/proxy protections for RSC endpoints.

triage.fix: Patch Next.js/React, then verify whether App Router/RSC is enabled. Add ingress limits and reject malformed/oversized requests early.

items.title: next 15.1.3 – nextjs: Next.js Content Injection Vulnerability for Image Optimization
items.description: Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. In versions before 14.2.31 and from 15.0.0 to before 15.4.5, Next.js Image Optimization is vulnerable to content injection. The issue allowed attacker-controlled external image sources to trigger file downloads with arbitrary content and filenames under specific configurations. This behavior could be abused for phishing or malicious file delivery. This vulnerability has been fixed in Next.js versions 14.2.31 and 15.4.5.

items.title: next 15.1.3 – nextjs: Next.js Affected by Cache Key Confusion for Image Optimization API Routes
items.description: Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. In versions before 14.2.31 and from 15.0.0 to before 15.4.5, Next.js Image Optimization API routes are affected by cache key confusion. When images returned from API routes vary based on request headers (such as Cookie or Authorization), these responses could be incorrectly cached and served to unauthorized users due to a cache key confusion bug. This vulnerability has been fixed in Next.js versions 14.2.32 and 15.4.7. All users implementing custom middleware logic in self-hosted environments are strongly encouraged to upgrade and verify correct usage of the next() function.

items.title: next 15.1.3 – next: NextJS Denial of Service in Image Optimizer
items.description:
A denial of service vulnerability exists in self-hosted Next.js applications that have `remotePatterns` configured for the Image Optimizer. The image optimization endpoint (`/_next/image`) loads external images entirely into memory without enforcing a maximum size limit, allowing an attacker to cause out-of-memory conditions by requesting optimization of arbitrarily large images. This vulnerability requires that `remotePatterns` is configured to allow image optimization from external domains and that the attacker can serve or control a large image on an allowed domain.

Strongly consider upg

items.title: next 15.1.3 – next.js: Next.js: Unbounded next/image disk cache growth can exhaust storage
items.description: Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. Starting in version 10.0.0 and prior to version 16.1.7, the default Next.js image optimization disk cache (`/_next/image`) did not have a configurable upper bound, allowing unbounded cache growth. An attacker could generate many unique image-optimization variants and exhaust disk space, causing denial of service. This is fixed in version 16.1.7 by adding an LRU-backed disk cache with `images.maximumDiskCacheSize`, including eviction of least-recently-used entries when the limit is exceeded. Setting `maximumDiskCacheSize: 0`

items.description: Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. From 14.2.0 to before 15.5.16 and 16.2.5, applications using React Server Components can be vulnerable to cache poisoning when shared caches do not correctly partition response variants. Under affected conditions, an attacker can cause an RSC response to be served from the original URL and poison shared cache entries so later visitors receive component payloads instead of the expected HTML. An attacker could cause out-of-memory conditions by requesting large local assets from the /_next/image endpoint that match the images.localPatterns configuration (by default, all patterns are allowed). In affected versions, serialized script content was not escaped safely before being embedded into the document, which could allow attacker-controlled input to break out of the intended script context and execute arbitrary JavaScript in a visitor's browser. This vulnerability is fixed in 15.5.16 and 16.2.5.

In affected versions, malformed nonce values derived from request headers could be reflected into rendered HTML in an unsafe way, allowing an attacker to poison cached responses and cause script execution for later visitors. items.title: postcss 8.4.31 – postcss: PostCSS: Information disclosure and denial of service via crafted CSS input
items.description: PostCSS takes a CSS file and provides an API to analyze and modify its rules by transforming the rules into an Abstract Syntax Tree. An attacker who controls the CSS input can cause the host process to read any file readable by Node and leak the first ~10 bytes of its content through the resulting JSON.parse SyntaxError message. The bug also yields a precise file-ex

triage.explanation: PostCSS issues usually matter when processing attacker-controlled CSS input at runtime or in a service path, which many apps do not do. If PostCSS is only used at build time on trusted source files, production risk is low.
triage.fix: Upgrade postcss to a fixed version. Also ensure runtime code does not pass untrusted CSS into PostCSS process() and disable automatic source map loading where unnecessary.

items.title: postcss 8.4.31 – postcss: PostCSS: Information disclosure via path traversal in source map auto-loading
items.description: PostCSS takes a CSS file and provides an API to analyze and modify its rules by transforming the rules into an Abstract Syntax Tree. triage.fix: Upgrade postcss to 8.5.18 or later. Avoid processing untrusted CSS at runtime and disable or sanitize sourceMappingURL handling.

When user-submitted CSS is parsed and re-stringified for embedding in HTML `<style>` tags, `</style>` in CSS values breaks out of the style context, enabling XSS. Version 8.5.10 fixes the issue.

items.title: com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-core 2.17.2 – com.fasterxml.jackson.core/jackson-core: tools.jackson.core/jackson-core: jackson-core: Denial of Service via incomplete fix in async JSON parser
items.description:
The fix released in jackson-core 2.18.6 and 2.21.1 for CVE-2026-18401 (GHSA-72hv-8253-57qq, number length constraint bypass in the non-blocking parser) is incomplete. This record covers the remaining bypass.

The earlier fix wired validateIntegerLength() into a new _setIntLength() helper and invoked it wherever the integer portion of a number is decided: a terminator byte arrives, a '.' or 'e'/'E' is seen, or input ends inside a fully buffered value. It was not invoked on the attacker-relevant path where the parser runs out of input while still inside the MINOR_NUMBER_INTEGER_DIGITS minor stat

triage.explanation: The vulnerable jackson-core version is present, but this DoS path is tied to the non-blocking/async JSON parser, which many Spring MVC applications do not use. Applicability depends on whether the backend uses Jackson async parsing directly or through a framework integration.
triage.fix: Upgrade jackson-core to a fixed version. Also confirm whether async/non-blocking parsing is used; if not, document reduced applicability.

items.title: com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-core 2.17.2 – com.fasterxml.jackson/jackson-core: tools.jackson.core/jackson-core: Jackson-core: Denial of Service via regular expression backtracking
items.description:
NumberInput.looksLikeValidNumber() in FasterXML jackson-core pre-validates "stringified numbers" with two regular expressions: PATTERN_FLOAT ([+-]?[0-9]*[\.]?[0-9]+([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?), present since 2.17.0, and PATTERN_FLOAT_TRAILING_DOT, added in 2.17.2. PATTERN_FLOAT places adjacent quantifiers over the same character class -- an optional [0-9]* run, an optional dot, then a required [0-9]+ run -- so input that ultimately fails to match forces Java's backtracking engine to retry every possible split point of the digit run. 



Matching cost therefore grows with the square of the input length.

triage.explanation: This is a parser-level DoS in jackson-core affecting numeric string validation and can be triggered during normal JSON processing if attacker-controlled payloads are parsed. Since a backend API commonly accepts JSON from users, this is plausibly reachable.
triage.fix: Upgrade jackson-core to a fixed version. Add request size/time limits at the reverse proxy and application layer to reduce parser abuse impact.

Unlike the three sibling parser implementations, including UTF8StreamJsonParser, it never consults ErrorReportConfiguration.getMaxErrorTokenLength() (default 256). A malformed token supplied to a parser created through JsonFactory.createParser(DataInput) is therefore accumulated in full. No StreamReadConstraints setting mitigates this: maxDocumentLength cannot be applied to Dat

triage.explanation: This malformed-token processing DoS is in core Jackson parsing and may be triggered by crafted JSON input sent to API endpoints. Because the application likely parses untrusted JSON requests, the issue is relevant even without special features enabled.
triage.fix: Upgrade jackson-core to a patched version. Enforce request body size limits and consider upstream rate limiting/WAF protections for malformed JSON floods.

items.description:
Improper encoding of non-finite floating-point values during MapMessage JSON serialization in Apache Log4j API produces output that is not valid JSON. This issue affects Apache Log4j API versions 2.13.1 through 2.25.4 and version 2.26.0.

items.title: org.apache.tomcat.embed:tomcat-embed-core 10.1.31 – tomcat: Potential RCE and/or information disclosure and/or information corruption with partial PUT
items.description:
Path Equivalence: 'file.Name' (Internal Dot) leading to Remote Code Execution and/or Information disclosure and/or malicious content added to uploaded files via write enabled Default Servlet in Apache Tomcat.

This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.2, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.34, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.98.
The following versions were EOL at the time the CVE was created but are 
known to be affected: 8.5.0 though 8.5.100. Other, older, EOL versions

If all of the following were true, a malicious user was able to view       security sensitive

triage.explanation: The vulnerable Tomcat version is present, but exploitation requires specific conditions: write-enabled DefaultServlet/partial PUT handling and typically an application that permits such writes. In a Spring Boot backend, this is often not intentionally enabled, so impact depends on runtime configuration.
triage.fix: Upgrade tomcat-embed-core to a fixed 10.1.x release. Also verify DefaultServlet is not write-enabled, disable partial PUT if not needed, and ensure no user-controlled uploads can be written into web-accessible/JSP-resolved locations.

items.title: org.apache.tomcat.embed:tomcat-embed-core 10.1.31 – tomcat-coyote: Apache Tomcat: HTTP/2 request headers not validated
items.description:
Improper Input Validation vulnerability in Apache Tomcat.

This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.21, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.54, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.117, from 10.0.0-M1 through 10.0.27.
Older, end of support versions may also be affected.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version [FIXED_VERSION], which fixes the issue.

triage.explanation: The affected Tomcat HTTP/2 component is in use by version, and malformed header validation flaws can be reachable whenever HTTP/2 is enabled on the server or upstream connector. Even if exploitability varies, this is a core protocol parser issue in the embedded server.
triage.fix: Upgrade tomcat-embed-core to a fixed 10.1.x version at or above the vendor-patched release. If immediate upgrade is not possible, disable HTTP/2 support until patched.

items.title: org.apache.tomcat.embed:tomcat-embed-core 10.1.31 – tomcat-coyote: Apache Tomcat: Authentication bypass via digest authentication
items.description:

Older unsupported versions any also be affect

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.22, 10.1.55 or 9.0.118 which fix the issue.

triage.explanation: This issue is specific to DIGEST authentication, which is uncommon in Spring Boot applications and usually not used when Spring Security handles auth with sessions, JWT, or basic auth. If the app does not configure Tomcat DIGEST authenticator, this finding is not applicable.
triage.fix: Confirm DIGEST authentication is not configured in Tomcat/web.xml/security constraints. If unused, document as not applicable; otherwise upgrade Tomcat to a fixed version and migrate away from DIGEST auth.

items.title: org.apache.tomcat.embed:tomcat-embed-core 10.1.31 – tomcat-coyote: tomcat: Improper Authorization allows security bypass
items.description:
Improper Authorization vulnerability when multiple method constraints define an HTTP method for the same extension in Apache Tomcat.

This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.21, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.54, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.117, from 8.5.0 through 8.5.100, from 7.0.0 through 7.0.109.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.22, 10.1.55 or 9.0.118 which fix the issue.

triage.explanation: This authorization bypass depends on servlet security-constraint method mappings for the same extension, a pattern more common in traditional web.xml-managed apps than typical Spring Boot APIs. It matters only if the application relies on Tomcat container-managed authorization rules rather than Spring Security request matching.
triage.fix: Review whether servlet security constraints or web.xml method constraints are used. If yes, upgrade Tomcat promptly and simplify/normalize overlapping method constraints; otherwise document as not applicable.

items.title: org.apache.tomcat.embed:tomcat-embed-core 10.1.31 – tomcat: Apache Tomcat: Security constraint bypass due to improper access control
items.description:
Improper Access Control, Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in Apache Tomcat leads to security constraint bypass if a constraint for a longer path is specified before a more restrictive constraint for a shorter sub-path.



This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.24, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.57, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.120, from 8.5.0 through 8.5.100, from 7.0.0 through 7.0.109.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.25, 10.1.58, 9.0.121, which fixes the issue.

triage.explanation: The issue requires specific ordering and overlap of Tomcat security constraints on URL paths. For a Spring Boot employee-management backend, risk is low unless access control is enforced through container security constraints instead of application-layer security.
triage.fix: Upgrade Tomcat to a fixed release. Audit any web.xml or programmatic servlet security constraints for overlapping path rules and ensure authorization is enforced in Spring Security/controllers rather than only container path constraints.

items.title: org.apache.tomcat.embed:tomcat-embed-core 10.1.31 – tomcat: Apache Tomcat: Authentication bypass via limited replay attack in DIGEST authenticator
items.description:

authenticated request with a nonceCount on the upper boundary of the

associated nonceCount remains within the replay window.



 

This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.24, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.57, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.120.

known to be affected: from 8.

triage.explanation: This is limited to Tomcat's DIGEST authenticator replay handling. If the application does not use DIGEST authentication, there is no practical exposure.
triage.fix: Verify DIGEST auth is disabled/not configured. If it is used, upgrade Tomcat and replace DIGEST with stronger modern authentication such as session-based auth behind TLS or token-based auth.

items.title: org.apache.tomcat.embed:tomcat-embed-core 10.1.31 – tomcat: Apache Tomcat: Unauthorized resource access via FORM authentication bypass
items.description:

triage.fix: Confirm the app is not using Tomcat FORM authentication or servlet security constraints. If it is, upgrade Tomcat and move authorization checks into Spring Security with explicit method/path rules.

items.title: org.apache.tomcat.embed:tomcat-embed-core 10.1.31 – tomcat: RCE due to TOCTOU issue in JSP compilation
items.description:

known to be affected: 8.5.0 though 8.5.100. Other, older, EOL versions may also be affected.

triage.explanation: The vulnerable Tomcat version is affected, but exploitation requires JSP compilation plus case-insensitive filesystem behavior and write-enabled DefaultServlet/non-default conditions. A backend service packaged as a Spring Boot jar often does not expose writable JSP paths, so runtime deployment details matter.
triage.fix: Upgrade Tomcat to a fixed release. Ensure JSP support is disabled if unused, keep DefaultServlet read-only, and prevent any upload/write path from landing in executable web roots.

items.title: org.apache.tomcat.embed:tomcat-embed-core 10.1.31 – tomcat: Apache Tomcat DoS in multipart upload

triage.explanation: Multipart upload DoS issues are commonly reachable in web backends that accept file uploads or multipart form submissions. For an employee-management application, uploads such as profile documents or attachments are plausible, so this should be treated as relevant unless multipart is definitively unused.
triage.fix: Upgrade Tomcat to a patched version. Configure strict multipart size/count limits in Spring/Tomcat and enforce reverse-proxy request body limits.

items.title: org.apache.tomcat.embed:tomcat-embed-core 10.1.31 – tomcat: http/2 "MadeYouReset" DoS attack through HTTP/2 control frames
items.description:

triage.explanation: This HTTP/2 DoS is relevant only if HTTP/2 is enabled between clients and the embedded Tomcat server. Many internal or simple deployments still use HTTP/1.1 behind a proxy, so exposure depends on deployment topology.
triage.fix: Upgrade Tomcat. If immediate remediation is needed, disable HTTP/2 on the application connector or terminate HTTP/2 at a patched front-end proxy.

items.title: org.apache.tomcat.embed:tomcat-embed-core 10.1.31 – tomcat: Apache Tomcat denial of service
items.description:

triage.explanation: The multipart integer-overflow DoS requires multipart handling and some less common configurations, so applicability depends on whether the backend accepts multipart uploads and how limits are configured. It is less certain than a generic parser flaw but still plausible.
triage.fix: Upgrade Tomcat. Review multipart configuration in Spring Boot/Tomcat, set conservative max-file-size/max-request-size thresholds, and reject unexpected multipart endpoints.

items.title: org.apache.tomcat.embed:tomcat-embed-core 10.1.31 – tomcat: Apache Tomcat denial of service
items.description:
Uncontrolled Resource Consumption vulnerability in Apache Tomcat if an HTTP/2 client did not acknowledge the initial settings frame that reduces the maximum permitted concurrent streams.

This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.8, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.42, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.106.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.9, 10.1.43 or 9.0.107, which fix the issue.

triage.explanation: This is another HTTP/2 resource-consumption issue and only matters when clients can speak HTTP/2 directly to Tomcat. If HTTP/2 is disabled or terminated upstream, practical risk is reduced.
triage.fix: Upgrade Tomcat to a fixed release. Disable HTTP/2 or place the app behind a patched proxy/load balancer that handles HTTP/2 safely.

items.description:

This introduced the       possibility that, for rewrite rules that rewrite query parameters to the       URL, an attacker could manipulate the request URI to bypass security       constraints including the protection for /WEB-INF/ and /META-INF/. triage.explanation: Directory traversal via rewrite requires use of Tomcat rewrite rules and specific URL rewriting behavior, which is uncommon in embedded Spring Boot apps unless custom RewriteValve/server config is added. It becomes serious only if such rewrite rules are present and can influence file/resource resolution.
triage.fix: Upgrade Tomcat. Check for RewriteValve/rewrite.config usage in embedded server customization; if present, remove risky query-to-path rewrites and normalize/decode paths safely.

items.title: org.apache.tomcat.embed:tomcat-embed-core 10.1.31 – tomcat: Apache Tomcat: Certificate revocation bypass due to improper OCSP response validation

known to be affect

triage.explanation: This OCSP validation issue affects Tomcat Native or the FFM port when using OCSP responder-based certificate validation. Most Spring Boot backends with embedded Tomcat do not use Tomcat Native plus custom mutual TLS/OCSP validation in-process.
triage.fix: Verify Tomcat Native/FFM and OCSP responder validation are not used. If they are, upgrade to a fixed Tomcat release and review TLS certificate validation settings.

items.title: org.springframework.boot:spring-boot 3.3.5 – org.springframework.boot/spring-boot: Spring Boot EndpointRequest.to() creates wrong matcher if actuator endpoint is not exposed
items.description:
EndpointRequest.to() creates a matcher for null/** if the actuator endpoint, for which the EndpointRequest has been created, is disabled or not exposed.

Your application may be affected by this if all the following conditions are met:

  *  You use Spring Security
  *  EndpointRequest.to() has been used in a Spring Security chain configuration
  *  The endpoint which EndpointRequest references is disabled or not exposed via web
  *  Your application handles requests to /null and this path needs protection


You are not affected if any of the following is true:

  *  You don't use Spring Secur

items.title: org.springframework.boot:spring-boot 3.3.5 – Spring Boot: Spring Boot: Arbitrary Code Execution and Session Hijacking via predictable temporary directory
items.description:
A local attacker on the same host as the application may be able to take control of the directory used by `ApplicationTemp`. When `server.servlet.session.persistent` is set to `true` and the attack persists across application restarts, this may allow the attacker to read session information and hijack authenticated users or deploy a gadget chain and execute code as the application's user.

Affected: Spring Boot 4.0.0–4.0.5 (fix 4.0.6), 3.5.0–3.5.13 (fix 3.5.14), 3.4.0–3.4.15 (fix 3.4.16), 3.3.0–3.3.18 (fix 3.3.19), 2.7.0–2.7.32 (fix 2.7.33); predictable temp directory / `ApplicationTemp` owner

items.title: org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-autoconfigure 3.3.5 – spring-boot: Spring Boot: Local attacker can manipulate data directory due to predictable path
items.description:
Spring Boot's ArtemisEmbeddedConfigurationFactory uses a fixed, static path for the embedded Artemis message broker's data directory when no explicit path is configured. A local attacker on the same host can pre-create this predictable directory or place a symlink before the application starts.

Affected versions:
Spring Boot 4.0.0 through 4.0.6; 3.5.0 through 3.5.14; 3.4.0 through 3.4.16; 3.3.0 through 3.3.19; 2.7.0 through 2.7.33.

items.title: org.springframework.data:spring-data-commons 3.3.5 – Spring Data Commons: Spring Data Commons: Denial of Service due to cache exhaustion via attacker-supplied strings
items.description:
Spring Data's internal property-lookup cache accepts and permanently retains attacker-supplied strings as cache keys, allowing heap exhaustion through repeated requests.

Affected versions:
Spring Data Commons 2.7.0 through 2.7.19; 3.3.0 through 3.3.16; 3.4.0 through 3.4.14; 3.5.0 through 3.5.11; 4.0.0 through 4.0.5.

items.title: org.springframework.data:spring-data-commons 3.3.5 – Spring Data Commons: Spring Data Commons: Denial of Service via parsing Sort parameters
items.description:
Applications using Spring Data Commons may be vulnerable to a Denial of Service (DoS) attack leading to a StackOverflowException when parsing Sort parameters.

Affected versions:
Spring Data Commons 4.0.0 through 4.0.5; 3.5.0 through 3.5.11; 3.4.0 through 3.4.14; 3.3.0 through 3.3.16; 3.2.0 through 3.2.15; 3.1.0 through 3.1.14; 3.0.0 through 3.0.15; 2.7.0 through 2.7.19.

items.title: org.springframework.data:spring-data-commons 3.3.5 – Spring Data Commons: Spring Data Commons: Denial of Service via specially crafted HTTP request with @ProjectedPayload
items.description:
Spring Data Commons contains a vulnerability that can lead to a Denial of Service (DoS) condition if Spring Data Web Support is enabled in conjunction with a Controller method using @ProjectedPayload, when an attacker sends a specially crafted HTTP request that causes the application to allocate lots of memory.

Affected versions:
Spring Data Commons 4.0.0 through 4.0.5; 3.5.0 through 3.5.11; 3.4.0 through 3.4.14; 3.3.0 through 3.3.16; 3.2.0 through 3.2.15; 3.1.0 through 3.1.14; 3.0.0 through 3.0.15; 2.7.0 through 2.7.19.

items.title: org.springframework.security:spring-security-core 6.3.4 – spring-security: authorization bypass for case sensitive comparisons
items.description: The usage of String.toLowerCase() and String.toUpperCase() has some Locale dependent exceptions that could potentially result in authorization rules not working properly.

items.title: org.springframework.security:spring-security-core 6.3.4 – Spring Security: Spring Security: Timing attack defense bypass allows information disclosure
items.description: Vulnerability in Spring Spring Security. If an application is using the UserDetails#isEnabled, #isAccountNonExpired, or #isAccountNonLocked user attributes, to enable, expire, or lock users, then DaoAuthenticationProvider's timing attack defense can be bypassed for users who are disabled, expired, or locked.This issue affects Spring Security: from 5.7.0 through 5.7.22, from 5.8.0 through 5.8.24, from 6.3.0 through 6.3.15, from 6.5.0 through 6.5.9, from 7.0.0 through 7.0.4.

items.title: org.springframework.security:spring-security-crypto 6.3.4 – spring-security-core: Spring Security BCryptPasswordEncoder does not enforce maximum password length
items.description: BCryptPasswordEncoder.matches(CharSequence,String) will incorrectly return true for passwords larger than 72 characters as long as the first 72 characters are the same.

items.title: org.springframework.security:spring-security-web 6.3.4 – Spring Security: Spring Security: Security policy bypass and information disclosure due to unwritten HTTP headers
items.description:
When applications specify HTTP response headers for servlet applications using Spring Security, there is the possibility that the HTTP Headers will not be written. 
This issue affects Spring Security Servlet applications using lazy (default) writing of HTTP Headers:

: from 5.7.0 through 5.7.21, from 5.8.0 through 5.8.23, from 6.3.0 through 6.3.14, from 6.4.0 through 6.4.14, from 6.5.0 through 6.5.8, from 7.0.0 through 7.0.3.

triage.explanation: The vulnerable Spring Security version is present, but impact depends on whether the application relies on Spring Security's default lazy header writing for protections like CSP, HSTS, frame options, or cache control. If custom filters/response handling commit responses early, headers may be skipped and policy bypass becomes relevant.
triage.fix: Upgrade spring-security-web to a fixed release. Review security header configuration, add integration tests asserting required headers on success/error responses, and avoid response commits before Spring Security header writers run.

items.title: org.springframework.security:spring-security-web 6.3.4 – Spring Security: Open Redirect via Unvalidated Post-Login Redirect URL Stored in CookieRequestCache
items.description:
Spring Security's CookieRequestCache and CookieServerRequestCache store the pre-authentication request URL in a browser cookie so that users can be redirected back to their intended destination after a successful login. In affected versions, the full absolute URL is stored in the cookie and is used without validation as the post-login redirect target.

Affected versions:
Spring Security 5.7.0 through 5.7.23; 5.8.0 through 5.8.25; 6.3.0 through 6.3.16; 6.4.0 through 6.4.16; 6.5.0 through 6.5.10; 7.0.0 through 7.0.5.

items.title: org.springframework.security:spring-security-web 6.3.4 – Spring Security Vulnerable to Unauthorized User Impersonation when Using X.509 Client Certificates
items.description:
SubjectDnX509PrincipalExtractor does not correctly handle certain malformed X.509 certificate CN values, which can lead to reading the wrong value for the username. In a carefully crafted certificate, this can lead to an attacker impersonating another user.

Affected versions:
Spring Security 5.7.0 through 5.7.24; 5.8.0 through 5.8.26; 6.3.0 through 6.3.17; 6.4.0 through 6.4.17; 6.5.0 through 6.5.10.

items.title: org.springframework:spring-core 6.1.14 – org.springframework/spring-core: Spring Framework Annotation Detection Vulnerability
items.description:
The Spring Framework annotation detection mechanism may not correctly resolve annotations on methods within type hierarchies with a parameterized super type with unbounded generics. This can be an issue if such annotations are used for authorization decisions.

Your application may be affected by this if you are using Spring Security's @EnableMethodSecurity feature.

You are not affected by this if you are not using @EnableMethodSecurity or if you do not use security annotations on methods in generic superclasses or generic interfaces.

This CVE is published in conjunction with  CVE-2025-41248

items.title: org.springframework:spring-core 6.1.14 – spring-framework: Spring Framework: Regular Expression Denial of Service in AntPathMatcher
items.description:
Applications may be vulnerable to a Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) attack if an attacker is able to provide a pattern which is then directly or indirectly supplied to one of the following methods in AntPathMatcher: match(String pattern, String path), matchStart(String pattern, String path), extractUriTemplateVariables(String pattern, String path).

Affected versions:
Spring Framework 7.0.0 through 7.0.7; 6.2.0 through 6.2.18; 6.1.0 through 6.1.27; 5.3.0 through 5.3.48.

items.title: org.springframework:spring-expression 6.1.14 – spring-framework: Spring Framework: Denial of Service via specially crafted SpEL expressions
items.description:
Applications that evaluate user-supplied Spring Expression Language (SpEL) expressions are vulnerable to an Algorithmic Denial of Service (DoS). By providing a specially crafted expression, an attacker can trigger excessive resource consumption during evaluation, leading to application degradation or unavailability.

Affected versions:
Spring Framework 7.0.0 through 7.0.7; 6.2.0 through 6.2.18; 6.1.0 through 6.1.27; 5.3.0 through 5.3.48.

items.title: org.springframework:spring-expression 6.1.14 – Spring Framework: Spring Framework: Denial of Service via unbounded cache growth in SpEL evaluation
items.description:
Applications which accept user-supplied Spring Expression Language (SpEL) expressions may be vulnerable to a Denial of Service (DoS) attack if the evaluation of a SpEL expression triggers unbounded cache growth.

Affected versions:
Spring Framework 7.0.0 through 7.0.7; 6.2.0 through 6.2.18; 6.1.0 through 6.1.27; 5.3.0 through 5.3.48.

items.title: org.springframework:spring-expression 6.1.14 – spring-framework: org.springframework/spring-expression: Spring Framework: SpEL vulnerability allows unintended application logic invocation
items.description:
A vulnerability in Spring Expression Language (SpEL) evaluation logic allows for arbitrary zero-argument method invocation, even within restricted or read-only contexts, which may allow an attacker to invoke unintended application logic.

Affected versions:
Spring Framework 7.0.0 through 7.0.7; 6.2.0 through 6.2.18; 6.1.0 through 6.1.27; 5.3.0 through 5.3.48.

items.title: org.springframework:spring-web 6.1.14 – springframework: Reflected download attack in Spring Framework with non-ASCII headers
items.description:

In Spring Framework, versions 6.0.x as of 6.0.5, versions 6.1.x and 6.2.x, an application is vulnerable to a reflected file download (RFD) attack when it sets a “Content-Disposition” header with a non-ASCII charset, where the filename attribute is derived from user-supplied input.

Specifically, an application is vulnerable when all the following are true:

  *  The header is prepared with org.springframework.http.ContentDisposition.
  *  The filename is set via ContentDisposition.Builder#filename(String, Charset).
  *  The value for the filename is derived from user-supplied inpu

items.title: org.springframework:spring-webmvc 6.1.14 – org.springframework/spring-webmvc: Spring Framework: Remote Code Execution via improper path limitation in XsltView
items.description:
Use of XsltView in a Spring MVC application can result in SSRF and RCE attack if the application has an "/**" mapping that results in view rendering, and where the view name is not explicitly specified.
Spring Framework 7.0.0 - 7.0.8
Spring Framework 6.2.0 - 6.2.19
Spring Framework 6.1.0 - 6.1.28
Spring Framework 6.0.0 - 6.0.30
Spring Framework 5.3.0 - 5.3.49
Spring Framework 5.2.25.RELEASE and earlier

triage.explanation: This RCE/SSRF issue requires use of Spring MVC XsltView plus a broad '/**' mapping with implicit view rendering. An employee-management backend API is unlikely to use XSLT views at all, making this probably non-applicable.
triage.fix: Confirm XsltView is not configured and no controller returns user-influenced implicit view names. If any XSLT view support exists, upgrade spring-webmvc immediately and remove/lock down XSLT-based rendering.

items.title: org.springframework:spring-webmvc 6.1.14 – spring-framework: Spring Framework: Denial of Service when resolving static resources
items.description:
Spring MVC and WebFlux applications are vulnerable to Denial of Service (DoS) attacks when resolving static resources.

Affected versions:
Spring Framework 7.0.0 through 7.0.7; 6.2.0 through 6.2.18; 6.1.0 through 6.1.27; 5.3.0 through 5.3.48.

items.title: org.springframework:spring-webmvc 6.1.14 – org.springframework: Spring Framework: Cross-site scripting (XSS) via incorrect JavaScript escaping
items.description:
Due to incorrect escaping, the use of JavaScriptUtils.javaScriptEscape() may lead to JavaScript code injection in the browser, potentially resulting in a cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability.

Affected versions:
Spring Framework 7.0.0 through 7.0.7; 6.2.0 through 6.2.18; 6.1.0 through 6.1.27; 5.3.0 through 5.3.48.

items.title: org.springframework:spring-webmvc 6.1.14 – org.springframework/spring-webmvc: Spring Framework MVC path traversal vulnerability
items.description:
Spring Framework MVC applications can be vulnerable to a “Path Traversal Vulnerability” when deployed on a non-compliant Servlet container.

An application can be vulnerable when all the following are true:

  *  the application is deployed as a WAR or with an embedded Servlet container
  *  the Servlet container  does not reject suspicious sequences https://jakarta.ee/specifications/servlet/6.1/jakarta-servlet-spec-6.1.html#uri-path-canonicalization

items.title: org.springframework:spring-webmvc 6.1.14 – Spring Framework: Spring Framework: Information disclosure via Java scripting engine enabled template views
items.description: Use of Java scripting engine enabled (e.g. JRuby, Jython) template views in Spring MVC and Spring WebFlux applications can result in disclosure of content from files outside the configured locations for script template views. This issue affects Spring Framework: from 7.0.0 through 7.0.5, from 6.2.0 through 6.2.16, from 6.1.0 through 6.1.25, from 5.3.0 through 5.3.46.

items.title: org.springframework:spring-webmvc 6.1.14 – spring-webflux: Spring MVC and Spring WebFlux: Denial of Service via slow static resource resolution on Windows
items.description:
Spring MVC and WebFlux applications are vulnerable to Denial of Service attacks when resolving static resources.


More precisely, an application can be vulnerable when all the following are true:

  *  the application is using Spring MVC or Spring WebFlux
  *  the application is serving static resources from the file system
  *  the application is running on a Windows platform


When all the conditions above are met, the attacker can send malicious requests that are slow to resolve and that can keep HTTP connections in use. This can cause a Denial of Service on the application.

items.title: org.springframework:spring-webmvc 6.1.14 – Spring Framework: Spring MVC and WebFlux applications: Information Disclosure via static resource resolution
items.description:

items.description:

items.title: bash 5.2.37-2+b5 – [Privilege escalation possible to other user than root]
bsdutils 1:2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: TOCTOU in the mount program when applying post-mount ownership/mode changes
items.description: A flaw was found in util-linux. When an /etc/fstab entry uses the user option together with X-mount.owner, X-mount.group, or X-mount.mode, mount(8) changes ownership or permissions on the mount target after mounting without re-verifying the path. A local unprivileged user can exploit this Time-of-Check-Time-of-Use (TOCTOU) window by swapping the target directory, redirecting the ownership/permission change to an arbitrary file and potentially escalating privileges to root.

items.title: bsdutils 1:2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: TOCTOU in the mount program via ancestor directory swap on target path
items.description: When an /etc/fstab entry is configured with the user or users option, mount(8) validates the target path before performing the mount syscall, creating a Time-of-Check-Time-of-Use (TOCTOU) window. A local unprivileged user with write access to an ancestor directory of the mount target can swap that directory to redirect the mount to an arbitrary root-owned location, potentially escalating privileges to root.

items.title: bsdutils 1:2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: SUID mount(8) allows nosuid/noexec bypass via LIBMOUNT_FORCE_MOUNT2
items.description: A flaw was found in util-linux. The mount(8) SUID binary does not sanitize the LIBMOUNT_FORCE_MOUNT2 environment variable before use. A local unprivileged user can set this variable to force mount(8) to use the legacy two-step mount(2) code path, which applies security restrictions such as nosuid and noexec after the mount is already active. During this window, an attacker can execute a SUID binary from the mounted filesystem, allowing local privilege escalation to root.

items.title: bsdutils 1:2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: failed external mount helper still runs privileged X-mount post-hooks
items.description: util-linux versions through 2.41.5 and 2.42.2 fail to check mount helper exit status before running post-mount hooks, allowing unprivileged users to execute privileged operations on pre-existing filesystems. Attackers can exploit X-mount.idmap or X-mount.owner hooks to clone filesystems with inherited suid bits or modify target inode permissions after a helper fails, achieving privilege escalation.

items.title: bsdutils 1:2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: nsenter --join-cgroup leaks root cgroup migration authority
items.description: The nsenter --join-cgroup option opens the target cgroup.procs file as root and leaves that file descriptor open across later namespace and credential changes and across execve(). Because the kernel checks later cgroup migrations using the credentials from the original open, a program run in an attacker-controlled target can inherit root's ability to move host processes between cgroups. After a privileged operator uses --join-cgroup against that target, an unprivileged user can migrate and terminate unrelated root processes.

items.title: bsdutils 1:2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: X-mount.subdir detached-tree resolution can escape via intermediate symlinks
items.description: The X-mount.subdir option uses a detached-tree fast path on Linux 6.15 and later and passes the configured subdirectory to open_tree() with AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW. That flag does not stop intermediate symlink traversal or keep resolution inside the newly mounted filesystem. A local unprivileged user with an fstab-authorized X-mount.subdir entry can attach a host path at the intended mountpoint.

items.title: bsdutils 1:2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: restricted bind mounts do not pin the source, allowing X-mount.owner/group/mode redirection
items.description: A flaw was found in util-linux. Restricted bind mounts take the source path from fstab but do not pin that source before the privileged mount. A local unprivileged user who can replace the authorized source or a writable ancestor can redirect SUID mount(8) to bind another host directory. If the fstab entry also sets X-mount.owner, X-mount.group, or X-mount.mode, root then changes ownership or mode on that redirected inode.

items.title: libacl1 2.3.2-2+b1 – acl: Symlink traversal privilege escalation via libacl functions

Attackers who control any component of a pathname processed by a privileged caller can redirect ACL read or write operations to arbitrary files or directories, enabling unauthorized manipulation of access control lists and local privilege escalation.

items.title: libacl1 2.3.2-2+b1 – acl: TOCTOU Symlink Traversal via getfacl/setfacl

Attackers who control a pathname component can redirect file access control list operations to arbitrary files when getfacl, setfacl, or chacl is invoked by a privileged process over an attacker-controlled path, resulting in local privilege escalation.

items.title: libblkid1 2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: TOCTOU in the mount program when applying post-mount ownership/mode changes
items.description: A flaw was found in util-linux. A local unprivileged user can exploit this Time-of-Check-Time-of-Use (TOCTOU) window by swapping the target directory, redirecting the ownership/permission change to an arbitrary file and potentially escalating privileges to root.

items.title: libblkid1 2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: TOCTOU in the mount program via ancestor directory swap on target path
items.description: When an /etc/fstab entry is configured with the user or users option, mount(8) validates the target path before performing the mount syscall, creating a Time-of-Check-Time-of-Use (TOCTOU) window. A local unprivileged user with write access to an ancestor directory of the mount target can swap that directory to redirect the mount to an arbitrary root-owned location, potentially escalating privileges to root.

items.title: libblkid1 2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: SUID mount(8) allows nosuid/noexec bypass via LIBMOUNT_FORCE_MOUNT2

A local unprivileged user can set this variable to force mount(8) to use the legacy two-step mount(2) code path, which applies security restrictions such as nosuid and noexec after the mount is already active. During this window, an attacker can execute a SUID binary from the mounted filesystem, allowing local privilege escalation to root.

items.description:
Passing an effectively empty string to the `,ccs=` syntax extension of the mode argument in the `fopen` function in the GNU C Library version 2.45 or earlier may result in a heap buffer overflow when the mode string input to the function is attacker controlled.



This usage pattern is not seen in applications in common GNU/Linux distributions and applications that process user-supplied values for `ccs` should not pass them through without validation.

items.title: libc-bin 2.41-12 – glibc: Buffer Overflow in strfmon right-justification padding
items.description:
Calling strfmon and strfmon_l in the GNU C Library version 2.38 to 2.44 can write past the end of the caller-supplied output buffer when a conversion uses right-justified width padding.

Exploitation requires an application code path that calls strfmon or strfmon_l with right-justified width padding into a destination buffer that is large enough for the padding to succeed but too small for the internal memmove call. The field width or format may be attacker-influenced or a fixed susceptible pattern in the caller.

At the time of publication, no network-facing application impact is known.

This vulnerability can be trivially mitigated by removing the IBM1390 and IBM1399 character sets from systems that do not need them.

This usage pattern is not seen in applications in common GNU/Linux distributions and applications that process user-supplied values for `ccs` should not pass them through without validation.

items.title: libc6 2.41-12 – glibc: Buffer Overflow in strfmon right-justification padding
items.description:
Calling strfmon and strfmon_l in the GNU C Library version 2.38 to 2.44 can write past the end of the caller-supplied output buffer when a conversion uses right-justified width padding.

Exploitation requires an application code path that calls strfmon or strfmon_l with right-justified width padding into a destination buffer that is large enough for the padding to succeed but too small for the internal memmove call. The field width or format may be attacker-influenced or a fixed susceptible pattern in the caller.

At the time of publication, no network-facing application impact is known.

This vulnerability can be trivially mitigated by removing the IBM1390 and IBM1399 character sets from systems that do not need them.

items.title: libcap2 1:2.75-10+b1 – libcap: libcap: Privilege escalation via TOCTOU race condition in cap_set_file()
items.description: A flaw was found in libcap. A local unprivileged user can exploit a Time-of-check-to-time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition in the `cap_set_file()` function. This allows an attacker with write access to a parent directory to redirect file capability updates to an attacker-controlled file. By doing so, capabilities can be injected into or stripped from unintended executables, leading to privilege escalation.

items.title: libgcc-s1 14.2.0-19 – gcc-toolset-15-gcc: gcc: gcc-toolset-16: gcc: Denial of Service via use-after-free in binary heap erase_if
items.description: A flaw was found in GCC. When an application calls the erase_if function on a binary heap priority queue in libstdc++, the library reallocates storage but fails to update its internal entry pointer. An attacker capable of triggering this operation can exploit this use-after-free condition, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) via an application crash or potential memory corruption.

items.title: libgcc-s1 14.2.0-19 – gcc: libstdc++ integer overflow in `new` operator
items.description: A flaw was found in libstdc++. An integer overflow can occur when processing large inputs to the aligned operator new in the C++ library. This vulnerability could lead to an undersized memory allocation, potentially causing memory corruption or application instability.

items.title: liblastlog2-2 2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: TOCTOU in the mount program when applying post-mount ownership/mode changes
items.description: A flaw was found in util-linux. When an /etc/fstab entry uses the user option together with X-mount.owner, X-mount.group, or X-mount.mode, mount(8) changes ownership or permissions on the mount target after mounting without re-verifying the path. A local unprivileged user can exploit this Time-of-Check-Time-of-Use (TOCTOU) window by swapping the target directory, redirecting the ownership/permission change to an arbitrary file and potentially escalating privileges to root.

items.title: liblastlog2-2 2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: TOCTOU in the mount program via ancestor directory swap on target path
items.description: When an /etc/fstab entry is configured with the user or users option, mount(8) validates the target path before performing the mount syscall, creating a Time-of-Check-Time-of-Use (TOCTOU) window. A local unprivileged user with write access to an ancestor directory of the mount target can swap that directory to redirect the mount to an arbitrary root-owned location, potentially escalating privileges to root.

items.title: liblastlog2-2 2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: SUID mount(8) allows nosuid/noexec bypass via LIBMOUNT_FORCE_MOUNT2
items.description: A flaw was found in util-linux. The mount(8) SUID binary does not sanitize the LIBMOUNT_FORCE_MOUNT2 environment variable before use. A local unprivileged user can set this variable to force mount(8) to use the legacy two-step mount(2) code path, which applies security restrictions such as nosuid and noexec after the mount is already active. During this window, an attacker can execute a SUID binary from the mounted filesystem, allowing local privilege escalation to root.

items.title: liblastlog2-2 2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: failed external mount helper still runs privileged X-mount post-hooks
items.description: util-linux versions through 2.41.5 and 2.42.2 fail to check mount helper exit status before running post-mount hooks, allowing unprivileged users to execute privileged operations on pre-existing filesystems. Attackers can exploit X-mount.idmap or X-mount.owner hooks to clone filesystems with inherited suid bits or modify target inode permissions after a helper fails, achieving privilege escalation.

items.title: liblastlog2-2 2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: nsenter --join-cgroup leaks root cgroup migration authority
items.description: The nsenter --join-cgroup option opens the target cgroup.procs file as root and leaves that file descriptor open across later namespace and credential changes and across execve(). Because the kernel checks later cgroup migrations using the credentials from the original open, a program run in an attacker-controlled target can inherit root's ability to move host processes between cgroups. After a privileged operator uses --join-cgroup against that target, an unprivileged user can migrate and terminate unrelated root processes.

items.title: liblastlog2-2 2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: X-mount.subdir detached-tree resolution can escape via intermediate symlinks
items.description: The X-mount.subdir option uses a detached-tree fast path on Linux 6.15 and later and passes the configured subdirectory to open_tree() with AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW. That flag does not stop intermediate symlink traversal or keep resolution inside the newly mounted filesystem. A local unprivileged user with an fstab-authorized X-mount.subdir entry can attach a host path at the intended mountpoint.

items.title: liblastlog2-2 2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: restricted bind mounts do not pin the source, allowing X-mount.owner/group/mode redirection
items.description: A flaw was found in util-linux. Restricted bind mounts take the source path from fstab but do not pin that source before the privileged mount. A local unprivileged user who can replace the authorized source or a writable ancestor can redirect SUID mount(8) to bind another host directory. If the fstab entry also sets X-mount.owner, X-mount.group, or X-mount.mode, root then changes ownership or mode on that redirected inode.

items.title: liblastlog2-2 2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: heap use-after-free in libblkid nested partition probing
items.description: A flaw was found in the libblkid library of util-linux. When subsequent partition additions cause the array to be reallocated, this pointer becomes stale, leading to a heap use-after-free read. items.description: util-linux is a random collection of Linux utilities. items.title: liblastlog2-2 2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: Access control bypass due to improper hostname canonicalization
items.description: A flaw was found in util-linux. Improper hostname canonicalization in the `login(1)` utility, when invoked with the `-h` option, can modify the supplied remote hostname before setting `PAM_RHOST`. A remote attacker could exploit this by providing a specially crafted hostname, potentially bypassing host-based Pluggable Authentication Modules (PAM) access control rules that rely on fully qualified domain names. This could lead to unauthorized access.

items.description: A flaw was found in the util-linux chfn and chsh utilities when compiled with Readline support. The Readline library uses an "INPUTRC" environment variable to get a path to the library config file. When the library cannot parse the specified file, it prints an error message containing data from the file. This flaw allows an unprivileged user to read root-owned files, potentially leading to privilege escalation. This flaw affects util-linux versions prior to 2.37.4.

items.title: liblzma5 5.8.1-1 – xz: XZ Utils: Denial of Service via buffer overflow in index decoding
items.description: XZ Utils provide a general-purpose data-compression library plus command-line tools. items.title: libmount1 2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: nsenter --join-cgroup leaks root cgroup migration authority

items.description:

which can have various consequences including a Denial of Service.

items.description:

of the affected QUIC server process and a Denial of Service.

items.title: libuuid1 2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: TOCTOU in the mount program when applying post-mount ownership/mode changes
items.description: A flaw was found in util-linux. When an /etc/fstab entry uses the user option together with X-mount.owner, X-mount.group, or X-mount.mode, mount(8) changes ownership or permissions on the mount target after mounting without re-verifying the path. A local unprivileged user can exploit this Time-of-Check-Time-of-Use (TOCTOU) window by swapping the target directory, redirecting the ownership/permission change to an arbitrary file and potentially escalating privileges to root.

items.title: libuuid1 2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: TOCTOU in the mount program via ancestor directory swap on target path
items.description: When an /etc/fstab entry is configured with the user or users option, mount(8) validates the target path before performing the mount syscall, creating a Time-of-Check-Time-of-Use (TOCTOU) window. A local unprivileged user with write access to an ancestor directory of the mount target can swap that directory to redirect the mount to an arbitrary root-owned location, potentially escalating privileges to root.

items.title: libuuid1 2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: SUID mount(8) allows nosuid/noexec bypass via LIBMOUNT_FORCE_MOUNT2
items.description: A flaw was found in util-linux. The mount(8) SUID binary does not sanitize the LIBMOUNT_FORCE_MOUNT2 environment variable before use. A local unprivileged user can set this variable to force mount(8) to use the legacy two-step mount(2) code path, which applies security restrictions such as nosuid and noexec after the mount is already active. During this window, an attacker can execute a SUID binary from the mounted filesystem, allowing local privilege escalation to root.

items.title: libuuid1 2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: failed external mount helper still runs privileged X-mount post-hooks
items.description: util-linux versions through 2.41.5 and 2.42.2 fail to check mount helper exit status before running post-mount hooks, allowing unprivileged users to execute privileged operations on pre-existing filesystems. Attackers can exploit X-mount.idmap or X-mount.owner hooks to clone filesystems with inherited suid bits or modify target inode permissions after a helper fails, achieving privilege escalation.

items.title: libuuid1 2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: nsenter --join-cgroup leaks root cgroup migration authority
items.description: The nsenter --join-cgroup option opens the target cgroup.procs file as root and leaves that file descriptor open across later namespace and credential changes and across execve(). Because the kernel checks later cgroup migrations using the credentials from the original open, a program run in an attacker-controlled target can inherit root's ability to move host processes between cgroups. After a privileged operator uses --join-cgroup against that target, an unprivileged user can migrate and terminate unrelated root processes.

items.title: libuuid1 2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: X-mount.subdir detached-tree resolution can escape via intermediate symlinks
items.description: The X-mount.subdir option uses a detached-tree fast path on Linux 6.15 and later and passes the configured subdirectory to open_tree() with AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW. That flag does not stop intermediate symlink traversal or keep resolution inside the newly mounted filesystem. A local unprivileged user with an fstab-authorized X-mount.subdir entry can attach a host path at the intended mountpoint.

items.title: libuuid1 2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: restricted bind mounts do not pin the source, allowing X-mount.owner/group/mode redirection
items.description: A flaw was found in util-linux. Restricted bind mounts take the source path from fstab but do not pin that source before the privileged mount. A local unprivileged user who can replace the authorized source or a writable ancestor can redirect SUID mount(8) to bind another host directory. If the fstab entry also sets X-mount.owner, X-mount.group, or X-mount.mode, root then changes ownership or mode on that redirected inode.

items.title: libuuid1 2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: heap use-after-free in libblkid nested partition probing
items.description: A flaw was found in the libblkid library of util-linux. During nested partition probing, the BSD, Minix, Solaris x86, and UnixWare partition probers cache a raw pointer to a parent partition entry in a dynamically allocated array. When subsequent partition additions cause the array to be reallocated, this pointer becomes stale, leading to a heap use-after-free read. items.title: libuuid1 2.41-5 – util-linux: TOCTOU in the mount program when setting up loop devices
items.description: util-linux is a random collection of Linux utilities. Prior to version 2.41.4, a TOCTOU (Time-of-Check-Time-of-Use) vulnerability has been identified in the SUID binary /usr/bin/mount from util-linux. items.title: libuuid1 2.41-5 – util-linux: util-linux: Access control bypass due to improper hostname canonicalization
items.description: A flaw was found in util-linux. Improper hostname canonicalization in the `login(1)` utility, when invoked with the `-h` option, can modify the supplied remote hostname before setting `PAM_RHOST`. A remote attacker could exploit this by providing a specially crafted hostname, potentially bypassing host-based Pluggable Authentication Modules (PAM) access control rules that rely on fully qualified domain names. This could lead to unauthorized access.

items.title: libuuid1 2.41-5 – [Integer Overflow or Wraparound in libblkid/src/partitions/dos.c]
items.description: [Integer Overflow or Wraparound in libblkid/src/partitions/dos.c]

items.title: libuuid1 2.41-5 – util-linux: partial disclosure of arbitrary files in chfn and chsh when compiled with libreadline
items.description: A flaw was found in the util-linux chfn and chsh utilities when compiled with Readline support. The Readline library uses an "INPUTRC" environment variable to get a path to the library config file. When the library cannot parse the specified file, it prints an error message containing data from the file. This flaw allows an unprivileged user to read root-owned files, potentially leading to privilege escalation. This flaw affects util-linux versions prior to 2.37.4.
